Learn Osoni, one step at a time.

Build your first PHP page, then learn to save form data. You do not need to learn every framework feature at once.

Install Osoni →Explore the reference →

    PHP 8.3+ / Windows & Linux / Available offline

    New to frameworks? Start here

    1. Read the beginner learning path for basic terms and how to use code examples.
    2. Follow Install Osoni. Choose SQLite and your computer's operating system.
    3. Make your first page. You will connect a URL to a template and display a name.
    4. Continue with Build your first feature to save and display notes.

    Already comfortable with PHP frameworks? Use the feature chapters for complete examples, the CLI reference to look up commands, or the function reference to check method names, inputs, and return values. You do not need to read the reference from beginning to end.

    About this manual

    No Composer, no PSR autoloading, and no external PHP packages. All maintained explanations and examples are US English. Open this manual directly from disk; its styles, search, and printing work offline. JavaScript enhances navigation and code copying, but is not required to read it.

    Includes 98 framework classes, 543 declared public methods and protected relationship helpers, 2 global helpers, all CLI commands, and every example environment setting.

    Examples are learning material, not commands to run blindly against production. Replace example IDs, domains, and owner checks with application-specific values. Back up before schema changes.

    Build your first feature

    Goal: build a page where you can enter a note title, save it, and see your latest notes. You will create one controller, one template, and two routes. This is a local learning exercise: everyone using this page sees the same notes.

    Before you start: finish the installation guide and Your First Page. Use a fresh local project and a database containing only practice data. All file paths below start from the project root, the folder containing osoni. You do not need email, AI, Redis, or a separate database server.

    1. Check your local database

    If you followed the SQLite installation steps, your tables already exist. In a terminal in the project root, run:

    Terminal
    php osoni migrate:status

    Expected result: applied migrations show batch numbers, not OPEN. If any are open, run php osoni migrate on this practice database and check again. If configuration or extensions are missing, return to the installation guide rather than continuing through errors.

    The installation uses SQLite at database/app.sqlite. The bundled migrations already create a notes table, so this exercise does not need a new migration or model.

    Understand where code runs

    When you visit a URL, a route chooses a handler. In this example the handler is a method on a controller. The controller reads or saves data, asks a template to produce HTML, and returns that HTML in a response.

    1. routes/web.php connects /notebook to the controller.
    2. The controller uses $app->db for database work and $app->views for page display.
    3. The template displays the notes and the form. It does not run database queries.

    Osoni loads controller files explicitly with require_once. The generator creates a file, but you still need to register its routes. We will do both below.

    2. Create a controller

    Terminal
    php osoni make:controller NotebookController

    Open app/controllers/NotebookController.php and replace the entire file contents with the following code, including its opening <?php tag. Save the file. The constructor receives Application, giving this class access to the framework services.

    PHP
    <?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Controllers;

use Osoni\Application;
use Osoni\Request;
use Osoni\Response;
use Osoni\Validator;

final class NotebookController
{
    public function __construct(private readonly Application $app) {}

    public function index(Request $request): Response
    {
        return $this->page();
    }

    public function store(Request $request): Response
    {
        $errors = Validator::errors($request->all(), [
            'title' => 'required|string|min:2|max:120',
        ]);
        if ($errors !== []) {
            return $this->page($errors, 422);
        }
        $this->app->db->table('notes')->insert([
            'title' => $request->input('title'),
            'created_at' => gmdate('Y-m-d H:i:s'),
        ]);
        return Response::redirect('/notebook');
    }

    private function page(array $errors = [], int $status = 200): Response
    {
        return new Response($this->app->views->render('notebook.index', [
            'notes' => $this->app->db->table('notes')
                ->orderBy('id', 'desc')->limit(20)->get(),
            'errors' => $errors,
            'session' => $this->app->session,
        ]), $status);
    }
}

    What this code does: index() shows the page. store() checks that the title is text between 2 and 120 characters, then saves it. page() reads the latest twenty notes and renders the template we will create next.

    After saving, the browser is redirected back to the list (HTTP status 303), so refreshing does not save the note again. Invalid input returns the form with errors (status 422). The query builder passes values separately from SQL, helping prevent SQL injection.

    3. Register the routes

    Open routes/web.php and add these lines at the bottom. Keep existing routes intact. Do not add a second <?php tag.

    PHP
    require_once $app->root . '/app/controllers/NotebookController.php';
$notebook = new \App\Controllers\NotebookController($app);
$router->get('/notebook', [$notebook, 'index']);
$router->post('/notebook', [$notebook, 'store']);

    GET /notebook opens the page; POST /notebook handles the submitted form. The URL is the same, but the request method chooses a different controller method.

    4. Create the view

    Terminal
    php osoni make:template notebook.index

    Open app/views/notebook/index.osoni.php, replace its entire contents with the following, and save. The dot in notebook.index becomes a folder separator. {{ ... }} displays values safely as text; @csrf($session) adds the hidden security token required for this form.

    HTML
    <!doctype html>
<html lang="en-US">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>My notebook</title></head>
<body>
    <h1>My notebook</h1>
    @if(!empty($errors))
        <p role="alert">{{ implode(' ', $errors['title'] ?? []) }}</p>
    @endif
    <form method="post" action="/notebook">
        @csrf($session)
        <label for="title">Note title</label>
        <input id="title" name="title" required minlength="2" maxlength="120">
        <button type="submit">Save note</button>
    </form>
    <ul>
        @foreach($notes as $note)
            <li>{{ $note['title'] }}</li>
        @endforeach
    </ul>
</body>
</html>

    5. Run and check the feature

    Terminal
    php osoni routes

    Check that both GET /notebook and POST /notebook are listed. If your development server is not already running, start it with php osoni serve. Do not start a second server on the same port.

    1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/notebook (use your chosen port if different). You should see a heading, a title field, and a Save note button.
    2. Enter My first note and select Save note. The title should appear in the list.
    3. Refresh the page. The note should still be there without being added a second time.
    4. Try a one-character title. Your browser should block submission because of minlength="2". The controller also checks the length because browser checks can be bypassed.

    To exercise the server-side length check on this local practice page, temporarily remove minlength="2" from the template, save it, reload the page, and submit one character. You should see an error without a new row being saved. Restore minlength="2" afterward. Keep the CSRF field in place.

    If you get 404, check the routes and URL. If you get 419, reload the form and submit again with cookies enabled. For a server error, check the server terminal and run php osoni logs:tail 20 error in another terminal. Keep those logs private.

    Next: move from demo to application

    Stop here if you are just learning. You have built the complete local example. The following steps are design work needed before making a real private notebook; adding a login check alone is not enough.

    Wrap both handlers with $app->auth->protect(...) if login is required. Add a new migration for a note-owner column and scope every read/write to the authenticated owner. The guard checks identity/verification, not object ownership. For public forms, also integrate the purpose-bound CAPTCHA/honeypot workflow from its chapter. Do not deploy the unscoped learning feature as a private notebook.

    PHP
    $router->get('/notebook', $app->auth->protect([$notebook, 'index']));
$router->post('/notebook', $app->auth->protect([$notebook, 'store']));

    Use these guarded registrations instead of the unguarded ones, not in addition. The existing registration/login/verification pages are already wired; configure mail and run a worker so verification/reset emails can be delivered.

    Common service recipes

    These are separate examples for later, not more code to paste into the notebook. Learn one service at a time from its feature chapter; email requires its own configuration and delivery worker.

    PHP
    // Display an exact amount without using floating-point money.
$total = $app->format->money('1234.565', 'USD'); // $1,234.57

// Create a JSON export; authorize access before returning it.
$file = \Osoni\Documents\Documents::json(['total_display' => $total]);
$response = $file->download('summary.json');

// Log safe identifiers, not request bodies, passwords, or tokens.
$app->log->info('Summary created.', ['report_id' => 42]);

// Build and queue an email; delivery is a separate worker action.
$message = $app->mail->compose([
    'to' => ['ada@example.test'],
    'subject' => 'Your summary is ready',
    'text' => 'Sign in to view your summary.',
]);
$emailId = $app->mail->queue($message);

    These recipes illustrate separate tasks; do not queue mail while rendering a GET page. Perform side effects only in an authorized, validated action and use the queue worker deliberately.

    Every CLI command

    Run from the project root with php osoni on Windows or Linux. Names are arguments, not arbitrary paths. Generators reject traversal, invalid identifiers, Windows device names, and existing/conflicting output rather than overwriting work.

    Commands normally return exit status 0 on success; failures print an error and exit nonzero. Commands can create files, change the database, or send actual email. --force permits production migrations/rollback/seeding; it is not a universal overwrite switch. API commands do not accept it.

    scheduler:install

    Check native process prerequisites and explain registration, migration, and worker startup. Does not create files, run migrations, or modify environment values. No cron, Task Scheduler, Composer, or external broker required.

    Terminal
    php osoni scheduler:install

    scheduler:list

    Load explicitly registered schedules and list definitions and next occurrences. Application definitions remain authoritative; registry files are trusted executable PHP.

    Terminal
    php osoni scheduler:list

    scheduler:status

    Show schedules and safe queue runtime counts. Requires migrated background tables. No payloads are printed.

    Terminal
    php osoni scheduler:status

    scheduler:run

    Materialize currently due occurrences transactionally, execute eligible direct work, then exit. Queued work requires queue:work. A safety ceiling limits one invocation to 1000 direct executions.

    Terminal
    php osoni scheduler:run

    scheduler:work

    Run native scheduling continuously using --sleep=1..60, optional --max-jobs=N and --max-time=seconds. --once materializes schedules and processes at most one direct job. Uses child PHP processes, heartbeats, and durable claims. Supervise separately for restart after reboot.

    Terminal
    php osoni scheduler:work --sleep=1

    queue:work

    Run durable job processing. Options: --queue=default,emails, --sleep=1..60, --tries=1..100, --max-jobs=N, --max-time=seconds, --once. Registry types and JSON payloads only. Requires proc_open. Timeouts cannot guarantee arbitrary cross-platform descendant termination or exactly-once business effects.

    Terminal
    php osoni queue:work --queue=default --max-jobs=100

    queue:status

    Show safe work counts and operational state without payloads or credentials. Requires background schema.

    Terminal
    php osoni queue:status

    queue:failed

    List safe failed/uncertain job metadata, default limit 50; --limit=1..1000. Investigate uncertain effects before deciding whether to repeat work.

    Terminal
    php osoni queue:failed --limit=20

    queue:retry

    Retry one confirmed failed job by its 32-character hexadecimal ID. Requires --force in production. Does not silently replay uncertain work.

    Terminal
    php osoni queue:retry JOB_ID

    queue:retry-all

    Retry at most 100 confirmed failed jobs per call; uncertain work excluded. Requires --force in production. Review each job business operation for idempotency before replaying.

    Terminal
    php osoni queue:retry-all

    queue:resolve

    Explicitly resolve uncertain work by retry or complete; always requires --force. First fence the old execution and verify external effects. The flag is an operator assertion, not evidence that a remote process died.

    Terminal
    php osoni queue:resolve JOB_ID retry --force

    queue:prune

    Remove bounded terminal job/attempt history with --days=1..3650 (default 30), --limit=1..1000 (default 100). Active/uncertain work must remain. Requires --force in production.

    Terminal
    php osoni queue:prune --days=30 --limit=100

    workers:list

    List worker IDs, type, host/PID, queues, heartbeats, and health. A stale heartbeat means suspected offline, not confirmed dead.

    Terminal
    php osoni workers:list

    workers:stop

    Persist a graceful stop request for a 32-character hexadecimal worker ID. Stops new claims and allows active work to finish; does not forcibly kill arbitrary PHP.

    Terminal
    php osoni workers:stop WORKER_ID

    about

    Print the framework identity (no release version is currently declared), PHP version, OS family, CLI SAPI, environment, database/cache driver names, session handler, and loaded extensions. Does not connect to services, print credentials/paths, or create storage. This describes CLI PHP, not necessarily the web runtime. No arguments/options.

    Terminal
    php osoni about

    env:check

    Compare .env key names with active/commented settings in .env.example, honoring process overrides. Print SET, EMPTY, MISSING, OPTIONAL, or CUSTOM and names only, never values. Exit 1 for missing active example keys, otherwise 0; empty/optional/custom entries need human review, not automatic failure. Reject malformed/duplicate local keys. Does not modify Env state/files or validate production readiness. Bootstrap must already succeed; use doctor for semantic checks. No options.

    Terminal
    php osoni env:check

    cache:test

    Write/read/delete one cryptographically random namespaced cache key with a 30-second TTL. No flush, database access, or application-key deletion. Requires an enabled reachable native Redis/Memcached backend; disabled or failed operations throw and the CLI exits 1. Cleanup runs after successful writes; interrupted/uncertain writes expire. Success prints no key, value, host, or credentials. No arguments/options.

    Terminal
    php osoni cache:test

    logs:tail

    Print up to 1..1000 most-recent matching JSONL records, default 50, in chronological order across daily files in configured private storage. Optional second argument is a lowercase minimum severity (debug through emergency), default debug. One-shot snapshot, not follow mode. Does not create storage or prune logs. Reject symlinks, invalid JSON/levels, entries above 64 KiB, and scans above 8 MiB instead of silently truncating. Re-encode terminal controls. Log messages/context remain confidential: restrict output and never pipe to public services. No options.

    Terminal
    php osoni logs:tail 100 warning

    make:command

    Create app/commands/Name.php returning a Closure(Application $app, array $arguments): int with a deliberately unimplemented body. Print an explicit registration entry for routes/console.php; do not auto-discover/import files or overwrite existing commands. Names use PascalCase ASCII letters/digits and cannot be Windows devices. Register a trusted unique lowercase command name; builtins cannot be overridden. Custom handlers receive raw remaining arguments, own validation/production guards, and must return an integer 0..255. No --force.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:command Report

    init

    Create .env from .env.example only if absent, with private platform-appropriate permissions. Existing configuration is preserved; no database or application key is created.

    Terminal
    php osoni init

    doctor

    Check production configuration, required/optional extensions, private storage, database/schema/migration readiness, encryption, SMTP configuration, and operational reminders. WARN mfa-enforcement prominently identifies emergency password/OIDC MFA bypass and gives restore/restart and existing-session guidance. Returns exit 1 if any check fails, otherwise 0; warnings need human review. Does not create storage/databases/tables, send mail, call AI, or test real web-server settings. Database connection and read queries occur only after storage checks pass. No --force.

    Terminal
    php osoni doctor

    storage:prepare

    Create the configured private storage root and logs, uploads, and views directories, plus files when the file-storage driver is local, using restrictive creation permissions. Existing files are preserved; symlinks and public storage are rejected. No remote provisioning, migration, file transfer, ownership change, or session/database relocation occurs. Run as the correct deployment identity; no --force.

    Terminal
    php osoni storage:prepare

    key:generate

    Print a fresh APP_KEY assignment. Copy it securely to .env yourself; files are not changed. Replacing a key makes older encrypted data unreadable unless you plan a migration.

    Terminal
    php osoni key:generate

    serve

    Start the native localhost development server, default port 8000, or a supplied 1024..65535 port. Runs in the foreground until stopped. Never use as a production server.

    Terminal
    php osoni serve 8080

    routes

    Load web/API route registries and print method/path pairs. Duplicate imports or invalid routes fail rather than being ignored.

    Terminal
    php osoni routes

    make:controller

    Create a controller skeleton under app/controllers. Explicitly require it and register its actions in routes/web.php; generating a controller does not expose a URL.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:controller ContactController

    make:test

    Create tests/application/NameTest.php for the native test runner; append Test when absent. Print an explicit require line for tests/application.php instead of editing the registry or discovering files. The generated test deliberately fails until replaced with assertions using check(), same(), or raises(). PascalCase ASCII names only; no overwrite, --force, or additional options. Run registered tests with php osoni test; no PHPUnit/Composer dependency.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:test ContactTest

    make:api

    Create API controller, route module, explicit registry import, and OpenAPI metadata together. Default resource actions are bearer-protected 501 placeholders; implement authorization and actual persistence before use.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:api Products

    api:token

    Issue a bearer token for an existing verified user. Optional name defaults to cli; days defaults to 30 and accepts 1..365. Trusted CLI issuance does not prompt for the user TOTP code; protect terminal access. The secret is printed once: do not log/share it or paste it into source control.

    Terminal
    php osoni api:token 1 integration 30

    api:tokens

    List token metadata for the supplied user ID, not token secrets. Use IDs from this list to revoke a token.

    Terminal
    php osoni api:tokens 1

    api:revoke

    Revoke the token identified by its token-row ID, not user ID. Already-issued clients will subsequently receive unauthorized responses.

    Terminal
    php osoni api:revoke 12

    api:openapi

    Print the registered OpenAPI JSON document to stdout. This still works with public API docs disabled. Shell redirection creates a file; keep export paths trusted.

    Terminal
    php osoni api:openapi

    make:model

    Create an explicitly loaded Model subclass under app/models. Configure the correct table, fillable, hidden, and casts before using it. It does not create or alter a database table.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:model Article

    make:view

    Create a plain PHP view using a dot-separated name. Render it through View, escaping values with e(); no route is registered.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:view articles.index

    make:template

    Create a compiled Osoni .osoni.php source template. The first render compiles it into storage/views. No Node/npm build or route registration is needed.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:template articles.index

    make:form

    Create a Osoni POST form view from one or more field:type arguments. Supports text, email, password, textarea, number, date, time, datetime-local, url, tel, and checkbox. Includes CSRF, labels, escaped old values, and accessible field errors; passwords are never repopulated. Pass session and a trusted local action URL when rendering, optionally old and errors arrays. Does not create routes, controllers, validation, or persistence. Existing PHP/Osoni views are never overwritten; --force is not accepted.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:form forms.contact name:text email:email message:textarea

    view:clear

    Remove recognized compiled Osoni cache files and print the count. Source views remain untouched; subsequent renders compile again.

    Terminal
    php osoni view:clear

    make:migration

    Create a timestamped migration with up/down methods. Fill in driver-appropriate schema SQL before migrating; generation itself does not connect or change schema.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:migration create_articles

    make:migration:import

    Create a timestamped migration from the configured database table structures, including columns, indexes, keys, and constraints, but not row data. Excludes Osoni migration bookkeeping. The generated DDL targets the same database driver and is for a fresh database; review it before use. Does not change the source database.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:migration:import import_legacy_schema

    make:seeder

    Create a seeder under database/seeders. Write repeatable inserts/updates deliberately. Seeders are executable trusted PHP, not validated user input.

    Terminal
    php osoni make:seeder ArticleSeeder

    migrate

    Apply pending migrations in order and print applied names. Production requires --force after a backup. SQLite/SQL Server/PostgreSQL DDL is transactional; MySQL DDL may not roll back.

    Terminal
    php osoni migrate

    migrate:status

    Print OPEN or BATCH numbers for discovered migrations, helping distinguish pending/applied schema work. Missing applied migration files are treated as errors.

    Terminal
    php osoni migrate:status

    migrate:rollback

    Run down() for only the latest batch in reverse order. May destroy data; production requires --force. Rollback is not a substitute for a backup.

    Terminal
    php osoni migrate:rollback

    db:seed

    Run the named seeder, or DatabaseSeeder when omitted. Production requires --force. Review the seeder first because it can change/delete data.

    Terminal
    php osoni db:seed ArticleSeeder

    mail:queue

    Read an existing JSON object file up to 6 MiB, validate from/to/subject/text/html, store a queued message, and print its ID. No SMTP is sent by this command.

    Terminal
    php osoni mail:queue message.json

    mail:list

    Print recent email metadata as JSON; default 50, accepted range 1..1000. Bodies are not listed, but subjects and delivery diagnostics can still be confidential.

    Terminal
    php osoni mail:list 20

    mail:show

    Print a complete stored email row as JSON by positive ID. Contains private message content; restrict terminal output, logs, and access.

    Terminal
    php osoni mail:show 12

    mail:send

    Claim/send one queued outgoing ID using SMTP, update its status, and report acceptance. Acceptance is not inbox delivery. Failed/uncertain rows require explicit retry handling first.

    Terminal
    php osoni mail:send 12

    mail:work

    Send queued IDs oldest-first in one bounded run, default 50, accepted 1..1000. Stop at the first failure. This is not a persistent daemon; schedule it with cron/Task Scheduler.

    Terminal
    php osoni mail:work 50

    mail:retry

    Requeue failed outgoing mail. --force also permits uncertain/sending recovery, which can duplicate delivery; stop active workers and check SMTP evidence first.

    Terminal
    php osoni mail:retry 12

    mail:fetch

    Read/import up to 1..1000 IMAP messages, default 50, without marking Seen or changing the mailbox. MAIL_LOG controls database import/deduplication.

    Terminal
    php osoni mail:fetch 10

    test

    Run isolated native tests, local HTTP, SQLite, local SMTP/IMAP, and AI HTTPS/SSE fixtures. No external email or AI requests are sent. Requires process/socket support and documented extensions.

    Terminal
    php osoni test

    help

    Print usage and the complete current command list. Also the default when no command is supplied. Unknown commands/options and excess arguments fail explicitly.

    Terminal
    php osoni help

    JSON input for mail:queue

    Create message.json yourself with a recipient list and at least one body. The configured MAIL_FROM is used when from is omitted. Do not commit real private message content.

    JSON
    {
    "to": ["ada@example.test"],
    "subject": "Welcome",
    "text": "Hello, Ada!"
}

    For a reviewed production migration, the explicit form is php osoni migrate --force. For an investigated uncertain email, php osoni mail:retry 12 --force can requeue it, but may duplicate delivery. Never combine either with an unreviewed deployment script.

    Environment reference

    The following defaults/example values come from the committed .env.example, never from a developer's real .env. System environment variables override the file. An empty value is not the same as a missing variable. Quotes remove only their outer delimiters; inline comments, interpolation, multiline values, and escape processing are unsupported.

    APP_NAME

    Example file value: Osoni

    Application name used in pages and API metadata. Default Osoni.

    APP_URL

    Example file value: http://127.0.0.1:8000

    Trusted base URL for authentication email links; its host also identifies the issuer/account label in authenticator MFA setup. Use the actual HTTPS origin in production; do not derive it from untrusted Host input. Existing app entries and queued messages are not renamed or rewritten by changing this value.

    APP_ENV

    Example file value: local

    local, testing, or production only. If absent, configuration defaults to production; the example file intentionally selects local.

    APP_DEBUG

    Example file value: false

    Boolean diagnostic web/API output flag. Plain-text exception/location/trace/request summary requires APP_ENV=local and true. Production and other environments always hide server-error details, even when this flag is true. Keep false in production.

    APP_KEY

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret base64:-prefixed 32-byte encryption key for encrypted model fields and authenticator MFA secrets. Empty disables usable encryption, not unrelated features. Generate securely; never commit or log it.

    AUTH_MFA_ENROLLMENT_ENABLED

    Example file value: true

    Allow starting and confirming new authenticator enrollment, true by default. False rejects both with 403, including pending setup; existing enrollment, challenges, recovery-code regeneration, and disabling remain available. Accepts only true/false (case-insensitive); empty/invalid values abort bootstrap. Restart all application processes on all instances after changes.

    AUTH_MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED

    Example file value: true

    Emergency-only local MFA login enforcement, true by default. False bypasses challenges for new password AND OIDC logins, retaining secrets/counters/recovery hashes; management still needs password plus second factor. Weakens account protection: restore true promptly. Does not revoke sessions/API tokens or promote pending challenges; bypass-created sessions survive restoring true until expiry/revocation. Accepts only true/false (case-insensitive); empty/invalid values abort bootstrap. Restart all application processes on all instances after changes.

    STORAGE_PATH

    Example file value: storage

    Private logs/uploads/view-cache/migration-lock directory, default storage relative to the project root. Also holds SQLite database-session lock files, not payloads. Absolute local paths support persistent data across releases. No dot segments, stream wrappers, symlink ancestors, public paths, or ancestors of public are allowed. Run storage:prepare; migrate existing files explicitly. Does not relocate SQLite databases or native PHP sessions.

    STORAGE_DRIVER

    Example file value: local

    File-storage backend: local (default), sftp, s3, or azure. Local uses STORAGE_PATH/files; remote selection does not relocate logs/uploads/views/sessions or migrate existing files.

    STORAGE_MAX_BYTES

    Example file value: 16777216

    Maximum bytes for file-storage put/get, 1..268435456, default 16777216 (16 MiB). Binary and empty content allowed; strings are buffered, not an unlimited streaming API.

    STORAGE_TIMEOUT

    Example file value: 30

    S3/Azure HTTPS request timeout in seconds, 1..300, default 30. Native SSH2 does not provide a guaranteed per-operation deadline; supervise SFTP separately.

    STORAGE_CA_FILE

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional readable local CA bundle for object-storage HTTPS. Empty uses system trust. Certificate/hostname verification cannot be disabled.

    STORAGE_SFTP_HOST

    Example file value: (empty)

    Trusted SFTP hostname/IP. Selected driver requires native ext-ssh2. Never accept endpoints from request data.

    STORAGE_SFTP_PORT

    Example file value: 22

    SFTP TCP port, 1..65535, default 22.

    STORAGE_SFTP_USERNAME

    Example file value: (empty)

    Least-privilege SFTP account. Server-side permissions/chroot are required for confinement against other filesystem writers.

    STORAGE_SFTP_PASSWORD

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret password authentication, mutually exclusive with configured key files. Leave empty for RSA PEM key authentication.

    STORAGE_SFTP_ROOT

    Example file value: (empty)

    Existing absolute remote directory, not filesystem root. Ancestors and entries must not be symlinks. Only child directories are created.

    STORAGE_SFTP_FINGERPRINT

    Example file value: (empty)

    Independently verified SHA-1 host-key fingerprint, 40 hexadecimal characters without colons. Required before authentication; no trust-on-first-use.

    STORAGE_SFTP_PUBLIC_KEY

    Example file value: (empty)

    Readable local public key file for RSA key authentication; requires matching private key and empty password.

    STORAGE_SFTP_PRIVATE_KEY

    Example file value: (empty)

    Protected readable local RSA private key in PEM format, at most 64 KiB. Generate using ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 3072 -m PEM. OpenSSH-format/ECDSA user keys are not supported.

    STORAGE_SFTP_PASSPHRASE

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional secret passphrase for the RSA PEM private key. Never print or log it.

    STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT

    Example file value: (empty)

    Trusted HTTPS origin for a path-style S3-compatible service, without paths/query/fragment/URL credentials. Example AWS origin: https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. Native ext-curl verifies TLS.

    STORAGE_S3_BUCKET

    Example file value: (empty)

    Pre-provisioned S3 bucket; no bucket creation or ACL changes. Permissions must allow the required object operations.

    STORAGE_S3_REGION

    Example file value: (empty)

    Explicit AWS Signature V4 region matching the endpoint/provider. No automatic region discovery or redirect following.

    STORAGE_S3_ACCESS_KEY

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret-access credential identifier for S3 Signature V4. Protect configuration and backups.

    STORAGE_S3_SECRET_KEY

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret S3 signing key. No SDK, credential discovery, or automatic refresh.

    STORAGE_S3_SESSION_TOKEN

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional session token for temporary S3 credentials; refresh externally before expiration.

    STORAGE_AZURE_ACCOUNT

    Example file value: (empty)

    Azure storage account name, 3..24 lowercase letters/digits. Default host is account.blob.core.windows.net.

    STORAGE_AZURE_KEY

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret base64-encoded 64-byte Azure account key for Shared Key signing. Not a SAS/connection string; Entra/managed-identity acquisition is not implemented.

    STORAGE_AZURE_CONTAINER

    Example file value: (empty)

    Pre-provisioned Azure Blob container. Uses BlockBlob writes; deletion includes snapshots and follows provider retention/version policies.

    STORAGE_AZURE_ENDPOINT

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional trusted HTTPS origin for Azure sovereign/custom hosts; empty uses the standard account host. No HTTP, URL credentials, path, query, fragment, or redirects.

    APP_LOCALE

    Example file value: en-US

    Default display locale for Formatter, en-US. Does not translate framework-maintained UI. Process environment overrides .env.

    APP_TIMEZONE

    Example file value: UTC

    Default Formatter IANA zone, UTC. No global PHP timezone change occurs.

    SCHEDULER_TIMEZONE

    Example file value: UTC

    Default scheduling IANA timezone; UTC by default. Calendar schedules may override it. Persistence uses UTC.

    SCHEDULER_POLL_INTERVAL

    Example file value: 1

    Native scheduler idle poll interval, integer 1..60 seconds; default 1. CLI --sleep overrides it.

    SCHEDULER_DUE_TOLERANCE

    Example file value: 5

    Allowed age of an occurrence under skipMissed(), integer 0..60 seconds; default 5. Does not enable historical replay.

    SCHEDULER_CATCH_UP_LIMIT

    Example file value: 100

    Maximum permitted runMissed(limit: ...) catch-up count, integer 1..100; default ceiling 100. Individual tasks default to skip.

    QUEUE_DEFAULT

    Example file value: default

    Default queue name, 1..80 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen; default default.

    QUEUE_TRIES

    Example file value: 3

    Default maximum total attempts, integer 1..100; default 3. Not three additional retries.

    QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL

    Example file value: 1

    Queue idle poll interval, integer 1..60 seconds; default 1. No busy loop on an empty queue.

    QUEUE_TIMEOUT

    Example file value: 300

    Default job execution timeout seconds, integer 1..86400; default 300. Not a guarantee to forcibly terminate arbitrary code on every platform.

    QUEUE_PRIORITY_AGING

    Example file value: 60

    Seconds of scheduling advantage per priority level, integer 1..3600; default 60. Older eligible low-priority jobs eventually outrank new high-priority jobs.

    QUEUE_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES

    Example file value: 65536

    Maximum encoded JSON payload bytes, integer 1..65536; default 65536. Payloads still require registered-type validation.

    WORKER_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL

    Example file value: 15

    Worker heartbeat period seconds, integer 1..60; default 15. Use a stale threshold comfortably longer than this interval.

    WORKER_STALE_AFTER

    Example file value: 90

    Suspected-offline threshold seconds, integer 10..3600 and greater than twice WORKER_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL; default 90. Staleness does not prove process death or authorize blind overlap-lock removal.

    SSO_ENABLED

    Example file value: false

    Optional single-provider OIDC browser login, false by default. Requires migrations and trusted HTTPS APP_URL/issuer. Local login remains available. Disabling does not revoke existing sessions.

    SSO_NAME

    Example file value: "Single sign-on"

    Escaped login-button provider display name, 1..80 characters when enabled; default Single sign-on.

    SSO_ISSUER

    Example file value: (empty)

    Exact trusted HTTPS OpenID Connect issuer, empty until configured. Must match discovery and signed iss. Entra requires a fixed tenant v2.0 issuer, not common/organizations.

    SSO_CLIENT_ID

    Example file value: (empty)

    Registered OIDC client ID, required when enabled. The exact APP_URL + /sso/callback URI must be registered at the provider.

    SSO_CLIENT_SECRET

    Example file value: (empty)

    Private OIDC client secret. Basic authentication is preferred, then client_secret_post; empty is allowed only for a provider advertising public-client authentication none.

    SSO_TIMEOUT

    Example file value: 10

    Per-request HTTPS deadline, 1..60 seconds, default 10. Includes response transfer; maximum response is 1 MiB. No redirect following or automatic retry.

    SSO_CA_FILE

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional readable local CA bundle for provider HTTPS. Empty uses system trust; certificate and hostname verification cannot be disabled.

    SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE

    Example file value: false

    Boolean Secure-cookie flag, false locally. Set true behind a properly configured HTTPS proxy; this does not encrypt an HTTP connection by itself.

    SESSION_DRIVER

    Example file value: native

    native (default) preserves PHP session.save_handler; database uses the application DB_* connection and migrated sessions table. Switching drivers logs users out. API requests and health/readiness probes remain session-free.

    SESSION_LIFETIME

    Example file value: 7200

    Database-session idle timeout in seconds, 1..31536000, default 7200 (two hours). Refreshes on every successful save, including unchanged sessions. Expired IDs are rejected even before garbage collection. Does not change native PHP expiry or browser-cookie lifetime.

    SESSION_LOCK_TIMEOUT

    Example file value: 10

    Database-session lock wait in seconds, 1..60, default 10. Requests for the same session serialize; timeout fails explicitly. SQLite uses bounded private storage/sessions file locks; server databases use connection-scoped advisory locks.

    API_DOCS_ENABLED

    Example file value: true

    Optional boolean override. Without it, HTTP Swagger/OpenAPI is enabled in local/testing and disabled in production. Static vendored assets remain public.

    DB_CONNECTION

    Example file value: sqlite

    sqlite, mysql, sqlsrv, or pgsql. PostgreSQL requires native pdo_pgsql/libpq; SQL Server requires PDO_SQLSRV and the Microsoft ODBC Driver. Live deployments need integration verification.

    DB_DATABASE

    Example file value: database/app.sqlite

    SQLite file path relative to project root, absolute local path, or :memory:. For server drivers, an existing database name. PostgreSQL names here are 1..63 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/dot/hyphen, starting with a letter, digit, or underscore. SQLite should not use SMB/NFS shared storage.

    DB_HOST

    Example file value: 127.0.0.1

    Server hostname or IPv4 address, default 127.0.0.1. Not used for SQLite. SQL Server/PostgreSQL use a separate TCP port, not named instances or Unix socket paths.

    DB_PORT

    Example file value: 3306

    Server TCP port 1..65535. Example: 3306 for MySQL; set 1433 for SQL Server or 5432 for PostgreSQL. When entirely absent, defaults follow the selected driver.

    DB_USERNAME

    Example file value: root

    Database login, root in the MySQL-oriented example. Set an appropriate SQL authentication login for SQL Server. Use least privilege in production.

    DB_PASSWORD

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret database password. Empty in the example, not a production recommendation.

    DB_MYSQL_TLS

    Example file value: verify_ca

    MySQL only: disabled (default, no SSL/TLS PDO options), required (encryption), or verify_ca (encryption and certificate verification). Both enabled modes check the negotiated cipher. All modes respect DB_HOST, including localhost, in every environment. For compatibility, required with a configured CA retains certificate verification.

    DB_MYSQL_SSL_CA

    Example file value: (empty)

    MySQL only: existing, readable local CA file required for verify_ca; use an absolute path such as /absolute/path/to/ca.pem. Also enables certificate verification with required for backward compatibility. Use a server certificate matching DB_HOST. Forward slashes are recommended on Windows.

    DB_ENCRYPT

    Example file value: true

    SQL Server only: true or false, default true. Encrypts the database connection. Keep true in production.

    DB_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE

    Example file value: false

    SQL Server only: true bypasses certificate verification, default false. Keep false in production and configure trusted certificates.

    DB_SSLMODE

    Example file value: verify-full

    PostgreSQL only: disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca, or verify-full. Default verify-full requires TLS and a trusted certificate matching DB_HOST. disable is for isolated non-TLS development only.

    DB_SSLROOTCERT

    Example file value: (empty)

    PostgreSQL only: optional readable local CA certificate file. Empty leaves root-certificate lookup to libpq. Use forward slashes on Windows; DSN delimiters are rejected.

    LOG_RETENTION_DAYS

    Example file value: 5

    Daily-file retention window, 1..3650 days, default 5. Includes today; pruning runs when an entry is written.

    LOG_LEVEL

    Example file value: debug

    Minimum lowercase severity: debug, info, notice, warning, error, critical, alert, emergency. Default debug. Higher thresholds may filter automatic error entries.

    UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES

    Example file value: 2097152

    Positive integer per-file default for the Uploads service, default 2097152 (2 MiB). Does not change PHP or proxy request limits; handlers can override.

    CACHE_DRIVER

    Example file value: none

    Optional shared cache backend: none (default, disabled), redis (native redis extension 6+), or memcached (native memcached extension 3+, not legacy memcache). No Composer; no session/rate-limit changes. Disabled or unavailable use throws, without fallback.

    CACHE_PREFIX

    Example file value: osoni:

    Application/environment cache namespace, default osoni:. Requires 1..64 ASCII letters/digits/colon/underscore/hyphen. Keys are SHA-256 hashed after this prefix. Not an authorization boundary; never share cache write access with untrusted applications.

    CACHE_TIMEOUT

    Example file value: 2

    Connection/read timeout seconds, integer 1..30, default 2. No application-level retry or fallback.

    REDIS_HOST

    Example file value: 127.0.0.1

    Single Redis server hostname/address, default 127.0.0.1. No URI, Unix socket, Cluster, or Sentinel discovery. TLS certificates must match this host.

    REDIS_PORT

    Example file value: 6379

    Redis TCP port, 1..65535, default 6379. Configure the actual TLS port when enabling TLS.

    REDIS_USERNAME

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional Redis ACL username. Requires REDIS_PASSWORD when nonempty; an empty username uses password-only AUTH.

    REDIS_PASSWORD

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret Redis password. Never log or commit it. Protect transport with TLS outside trusted networks.

    REDIS_DATABASE

    Example file value: 0

    Redis logical database index, integer 0..65535, default 0. Server must provide this database and allow SELECT.

    REDIS_TLS

    Example file value: false

    Boolean Redis TLS flag, default false for local development. True verifies peer certificates and hostname; verification cannot be disabled. Plaintext requires a trusted network.

    REDIS_CA_FILE

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional readable CA bundle for verified Redis TLS; empty uses system/PHP trust. Use forward slashes on Windows.

    MEMCACHED_HOST

    Example file value: 127.0.0.1

    Single Memcached server hostname/address, default 127.0.0.1. Binary protocol; no TLS in this adapter. Use a trusted private network or secured tunnel and never expose the server publicly.

    MEMCACHED_PORT

    Example file value: 11211

    Memcached TCP port, integer 1..65535, default 11211.

    MEMCACHED_USERNAME

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional SASL username, requires MEMCACHED_PASSWORD and a SASL-capable native extension/server. SASL authenticates but does not encrypt.

    MEMCACHED_PASSWORD

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret optional SASL password, requires MEMCACHED_USERNAME. Never log or commit it.

    AI_PROVIDER

    Example file value: openai

    Default server-side text AI provider: openai or anthropic (Claude), default openai. Individual calls can override it. No public endpoints are created.

    AI_TIMEOUT

    Example file value: 60

    Total native HTTPS deadline in seconds, 1..300, default 60. Includes connection setup and the complete stream; connect time is capped at 15 seconds.

    AI_MAX_TOKENS

    Example file value: 1024

    Default output token budget, 1..128000, default 1024. Per-model limits may be lower; reasoning models can spend budget on reasoning. Token-limit stop reasons remain explicit.

    AI_CA_FILE

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional readable CA bundle for native cURL. Empty uses system/cURL trust, including curl.cainfo. Never disables peer or hostname verification. Use forward slashes on Windows.

    OPENAI_API_KEY

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret OpenAI API key. Required only for OpenAI calls; API access and billing are separate from ChatGPT subscriptions. Never log or expose it.

    OPENAI_MODEL

    Example file value: (empty)

    Exact OpenAI Responses API model ID available to your API account. Intentionally empty: set it before calling OpenAI or pass a model override.

    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret Anthropic API key for Claude Messages. Required only for Claude calls; API access/billing are separate from Claude subscriptions.

    ANTHROPIC_MODEL

    Example file value: (empty)

    Exact Claude Messages API model ID available to your account. No default is assumed; configure before calling Claude or pass a model override.

    MAIL_LOG

    Example file value: true

    Boolean immediate-send logging/IMAP-import control, default true. Explicit queue() and auth mail always use the database queue.

    MAIL_FROM

    Example file value: noreply@example.test

    Default ASCII sender without a display name. Replace example.test with a valid authorized sender before real delivery.

    SMTP_HOST

    Example file value: (empty)

    SMTP server hostname/address. Empty until configured. Do not send through arbitrary user-selected hosts.

    SMTP_PORT

    Example file value: 587

    SMTP TCP port, default 587 for STARTTLS. Use the server-authorized port matching the selected encryption mode.

    SMTP_ENCRYPTION

    Example file value: starttls

    starttls, tls, or none. Default starttls; tls starts TLS immediately. none is restricted to unauthenticated localhost.

    SMTP_USERNAME

    Example file value: (empty)

    SMTP authentication username when required. Never log credentials.

    SMTP_PASSWORD

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret SMTP authentication password/app password. Protect .env and backups.

    SMTP_TIMEOUT

    Example file value: 15

    Native socket timeout seconds, 1..300, default 15. A timeout after DATA may leave uncertain delivery.

    SMTP_CA_FILE

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional readable CA bundle for peer verification. Empty uses system/PHP trust. Never disable verification to work around certificate problems.

    IMAP_HOST

    Example file value: (empty)

    IMAP server hostname/address. Empty until configured.

    IMAP_PORT

    Example file value: 993

    IMAP port, default 993 for immediate TLS. Match the server configuration when using STARTTLS instead.

    IMAP_ENCRYPTION

    Example file value: tls

    tls, starttls, or restricted none. Default tls; ordinary authenticated IMAP requires encryption.

    IMAP_USERNAME

    Example file value: (empty)

    IMAP account username. Used with encrypted LOGIN; not exposed in manual output.

    IMAP_PASSWORD

    Example file value: (empty)

    Secret IMAP password/app password. Never paste it into documentation or diagnostics.

    IMAP_TIMEOUT

    Example file value: 15

    Socket timeout seconds, 1..300, default 15.

    IMAP_CA_FILE

    Example file value: (empty)

    Optional readable CA trust bundle, otherwise PHP/system CA defaults are used.

    IMAP_MAILBOX

    Example file value: INBOX

    Read-only examined mailbox, default INBOX. ASCII or IMAP modified UTF-7 name, up to 255 printable ASCII bytes.

    IMAP_MAX_BYTES

    Example file value: 10485760

    Per-message retrieval bound, 1..52428800 bytes, default 10485760 (10 MiB). Batch retrieval is also bounded at 50 MiB.

    PHP and web-server settings are separate

    upload_max_filesize, post_max_size, max_file_uploads, upload_tmp_dir, session save paths, CA certificates, memory/time limits, error logging, and web-server body/TLS limits are not automatically set from these environment keys. Configure the PHP installation used by the actual web server, which may differ from CLI PHP.

    Troubleshooting

    Class not found
    Check exact filename casing and add an explicit require_once before using the class. Osoni intentionally has no Composer/PSR autoloader.
    404 or 405
    Run php osoni routes. Check the exact route, HTTP method, registry import, and web-server front-controller rewrite. Generating a controller/view does not automatically register it.
    419 Session verification failed
    Reload the form, keep the same session cookie, and submit the current hidden CSRF token or header. Login/logout/reset, successful MFA login, enabling/disabling MFA, and recovery-code regeneration rotate session state and the token. Multipart requests need CSRF too. A GET, HEAD, or OPTIONS request to a path that only has state-changing handlers returns 405, not a token error, because those methods never carry a token.
    422 Security check failed
    Use the new CAPTCHA challenge after every attempt. Keep the website honeypot empty and submit the correct form purpose within five minutes. A consumed code cannot be retried.
    401 on the API
    Use an unexpired, unrevoked bearer token for a verified user. Browser login cookies do not authenticate API requests. Password reset, enabling/disabling MFA, and recovery-code regeneration invalidate existing tokens. Issue replacement tokens only through a trusted, authorized workflow.
    Authenticator code is rejected
    Enter all six digits, including leading zeros, without spaces. Use the newest code for the correct account and synchronize the device and server clocks. Enrollment, login, disabling MFA, and recovery-code regeneration share replay protection: a code already accepted once cannot be reused. Wait for the next 30-second code, or use one unused recovery code for login/disabling/regeneration. Recovery codes cannot confirm initial enrollment.
    MFA setup or login challenge expired
    Setup lasts ten minutes; choose Start setup again and scan the new QR code or enter its new key. A login challenge lasts five minutes; log in again, or use Cancel login to start over. Password reset or another session-version change invalidates pending challenges/setup. Merely scanning a setup QR code does not enable MFA: submit a valid app code to confirm it.
    Cannot scan the authenticator QR code
    Use the manual Base32 setup key with SHA-1, six digits, and a 30-second period. On the same device, try Open in an authenticator app on this device. The QR image is generated locally as inline SVG; it needs no external service, JavaScript, or image extension. Custom pages must keep its black-on-white contrast and white border. Never upload the QR image or key to a third-party decoder or support request.
    Recovery codes or authenticator are lost
    If one unused recovery code remains, enter the complete 20-character lowercase hexadecimal code in the login code field. Recovery codes work once and are shown only immediately after enrollment or regeneration. Open My account, Manage multi-factor authentication, then Regenerate recovery codes without disabling MFA. Confirm the current password and an unused second-factor code; the CSRF-protected POST replaces all recovery hashes without replacing the authenticator, revokes older sessions/API tokens, and shows the new codes once. Custom handlers can call regenerateMfaRecoveryCodes() with equivalent protections. To replace an authenticator, disable MFA and enroll again when enrollment policy allows. If both factors are lost, use a separately designed trusted administrator recovery process. A password reset does not remove MFA. The global emergency enforcement bypass weakens every enrolled account and is not normal per-user recovery.
    413 uploading
    Compare UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES, handler overrides, PHP upload_max_filesize/post_max_size, multipart overhead, and proxy limits. Framework settings cannot raise PHP/server limits.
    415 on the API
    Send an application/json object, not form data or multipart uploads. Use normal web routes for native file uploads/downloads.
    429 Too many requests
    Honor Retry-After. Direct REMOTE_ADDR is used; clients behind a reverse proxy may share its IP. Do not disable rate limits to hide an upstream configuration issue.
    Unexpected 500
    Outside local debug mode, the application shows a generic HTML error page for browsers and INTERNAL_ERROR JSON for API/JSON requests. Inspect private storage/logs and PHP server logs; automatic entries record safe source location/class, not messages or arguments. For trusted local development only, APP_ENV=local and APP_DEBUG=true show plain-text diagnostics. Verify required extensions, permissions, environment validation, and schema status.
    Data mapping or validation fails
    Use entry-level map/filter for lists, whole-document transform for restructuring, and wildcard rules such as *.email for top-level records. Rule/DTO classes must be explicitly loaded. A single request record must be wrapped in a list before entry-level DTO mapping. Validation failures expose concrete field paths; they do not silently drop rows.
    Remote storage fails
    Check the selected native extension, provisioned bucket/container/root, credentials, TLS or pinned SFTP host identity, and provider permissions. Storage failures are exceptions, not empty content or false existence results. Changing STORAGE_DRIVER does not migrate existing files. Never disable identity verification to bypass an error.
    Missing extension
    Use php -m for CLI, and inspect the web PHP configuration separately. Enable the selected native PDO driver (SQLite, MySQL, SQL Server, or PostgreSQL), OpenSSL, iconv, mbstring as needed, Intl, zip, DOM, and fileinfo for the features/tests described. SQL Server also requires the Microsoft ODBC Driver; PostgreSQL uses libpq. Do not install Composer packages as substitutes.
    Email stays queued
    Configure SMTP and run mail:work. Registration/reset queue mail rather than sending it inline. Check delivery status; uncertain/sending recovery can duplicate messages.
    Verification link points to localhost
    Set APP_URL to the trusted public HTTPS base URL before creating new links. Existing queued messages retain their original content.
    Encrypted content will not decrypt
    Check the exact APP_KEY and authenticated context. Never generate a replacement key to fix unreadable existing data. Restore the original key from secure backup or perform a planned migration.
    Formatting differs between machines
    Compare explicit locale/time zone and installed ICU data versions. Nonbreaking spaces, localized digits, and punctuation are intentional. Never parse formatted money as database numbers.
    Template appears stale
    Run view:clear and check the view name/path. A .osoni.php view takes precedence over a same-named .php view. Templates are trusted PHP, not a sandbox.
    Log file is absent
    Storage is created only on a written entry. Check LOG_LEVEL filtering, write permissions, symlink restrictions, and PHP server diagnostics. Retention runs on writes, not a timer.

    Before production

    • Serve only public/, enforce HTTPS, set APP_ENV=production and APP_DEBUG=false, and configure secure cookies correctly behind a proxy.
    • Protect .env, private storage, database/backups, mail contents, and log files. Align Linux service/CLI ownership or restrict Windows NTFS ACLs.
    • Back up schema/data and encryption keys separately. Review every migration/seeder and test restoration before using --force.
    • For authenticator MFA, apply the MFA migrations, preserve APP_KEY, synchronize server time, verify QR/manual enrollment and recovery-code login with a test account, and define a trusted lost-factor recovery procedure. Never store setup QR images or recovery codes in logs or support tickets.
    • Guard private routes and apply per-record authorization; neither valid tokens nor random file keys grant object ownership.
    • Set upload/request/time/disk/user quotas; consider quarantine and malware scanning. MIME checks do not prove a document harmless.
    • Configure SMTP/IMAP certificate trust and schedule bounded queue workers without overlapping unsafe recovery tasks.
    • Keep public API docs disabled unless intentionally needed; do not enable credential persistence in Swagger.
    • Run the native suite and separate deployment-specific Windows/MySQL/SQL Server/PostgreSQL checks where applicable. A CI configuration is not evidence that a specific deployment was tested.

    Maintain this manual

    Terminal
    php docs/build.php
php docs/build.php --check

    The builder requires native DOM for link validation. It checks declared public-method coverage, explicit examples, syntax of reference snippets, all CLI commands, every example environment key, duplicate IDs, and internal/source links. Keep the HTML and local assets together. For local preview, serve only the docs directory on localhost, never the project root.

    Start Here: Your First Steps

    New to frameworks? Start with a local copy on your own computer, not a live website. You should be comfortable editing a file, saving it, and writing basic PHP variables and functions. You do not need to understand every feature in this manual before making your first page.

    Follow this learning path

    1. Follow the Detailed Installation Guide. Choose SQLite and the built-in development server. Follow either the Linux or Windows PHP instructions, not both.
    2. Check that the home page opens in your browser. Then follow Your First Page below.
    3. In the HTML manual, continue with Build your first feature to create a form that saves notes to a database.
    4. Read feature chapters only when you need them. Email, AI, Redis, external database servers, APIs, and production deployment can wait.

    The function reference is a lookup tool, not a course to read from beginning to end. If a method's technical details feel unfamiliar, return to its feature chapter for a complete example.

    How to read the examples

    • Terminal commands start with php osoni or another program name. Run them in PowerShell on Windows or a terminal on Linux, one line at a time. Wait for each command to finish; stop and fix any error before continuing. Do not paste these commands into a PHP file.
    • PHP and HTML examples go in the file named immediately above the example. Save the file, then refresh your browser.
    • Configuration examples go in .env, a hidden text file in the main project folder. Edit the existing setting; do not add a duplicate line. Never share this file because it can contain passwords and keys.
    • Project root means the main Osoni folder containing the osoni file. Run every php osoni ... command from there.
    • Example paths such as /absolute/path/to/osoni are placeholders. Replace them with the folder on your own computer. Do not type a shell prompt such as $ or PS> before a command.

    Words you will meet

    TermPlain-language meaning
    FrameworkReusable tools and structure so you do not have to build every website feature from scratch.
    CLICommand-line interface: commands you type in a terminal, such as php osoni help.
    RouteA rule connecting a URL and request method to the PHP code that handles it.
    GET / POSTGET requests read a page; POST requests submit data, such as a form.
    ControllerA PHP class that handles a request, uses services, and returns a response.
    View / templateA file that describes the HTML shown to the visitor.
    MVCModel, View, Controller: separate data work, page display, and request handling.
    MigrationA PHP file describing a database structure change, such as creating a table.
    SeederCode that adds starting or example data to a database.
    SQLiteA database stored in a file; it does not need a separate database server.
    Environment settingA named value in .env that configures this installation without changing application code.
    Local / productionLocal runs on your computer for development; production is a deployed site used by real visitors.
    CSRF tokenA hidden form value checked by the server to help prevent another site from submitting actions using your login session.
    EscapingDisplaying a value as text instead of allowing it to become executable HTML. Osoni's {{ ... }} does this for you.

    Your First Page

    Goal: display Hello, Ada! at /hello. This exercise needs no database queries, login, or email. Finish the local installation first and confirm that http://127.0.0.1:8000 opens.

    1. Create a template

    If the development server is running, leave it running and open a second terminal in the project root for commands. Alternatively, press Ctrl+C to stop it and start it again when you are ready to test.

    Run:

    Terminal
    php osoni make:template hello

    This creates app/views/hello.osoni.php. Open that file in your editor and replace its entire contents with:

    HTML
    <!doctype html>
<html lang="en-US">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>My first Osoni page</title></head>
<body>
    <h1>Hello, {{ $name }}!</h1>
    <p>I made this page with Osoni.</p>
</body>
</html>

    $name is a variable we will pass from the route. The double braces display its value safely as text. Creating this file alone does not create a URL.

    2. Connect a URL to the template

    Open routes/web.php. Add this code at the bottom, keeping the existing code. The file already begins with <?php; do not add another opening tag.

    PHP
    $router->get('/hello', static function (\Osoni\Request $request) use ($app): \Osoni\Response {
    return new \Osoni\Response($app->views->render('hello', [
        'name' => 'Ada',
    ]));
});

    This rule handles a GET request to /hello. $app gives the handler access to framework services. render('hello', ...) loads the template and passes it a variable named $name. Response sends the resulting HTML to the browser. The $request parameter represents the incoming request; this simple page does not need to read anything from it.

    3. Open and change your page

    If the server is not running, run:

    Terminal
    php osoni serve

    Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/hello. You should see Hello, Ada! and the sentence from your template. Use your chosen port instead if it is not 8000.

    Change 'Ada' to your own name in routes/web.php, save, and refresh. The heading should change. No compilation command is needed.

    If the page is not found, run php osoni routes in the second terminal and check that GET /hello is listed. If it is not, check that you saved the route in the same project copy that your server is running. If you see a server error, inspect the server terminal and run php osoni logs:tail 20 error. Check the example for missing brackets, quotes, or semicolons; do not publish private logs.

    You have connected a route to a view and passed it data. Next, use Build your first feature in the HTML manual to move request handling into a controller and save form data.

    Comparison with Laravel and CodeIgniter

    There is no best framework for every application. Osoni prioritizes explicit native PHP code without Composer; Laravel offers a broad integrated framework and package ecosystem; CodeIgniter offers a modular MVC framework with both manual and Composer installation options.

    Scope and review date: November 13, 2026. This compares the Osoni source shipped with this manual, Laravel 13.x, and CodeIgniter 4 using the official documentation linked below. CodeIgniter's online guide tracks its current release rather than a fixed patch version. Check the requirements of the exact release and packages you install. “Included” and “available through an additional package” are distinguished; neither means that a production application needs no configuration.

    Setup and everyday development

    AreaOsoniLaravel 13.xCodeIgniter 4
    PHP requirementPHP 8.3+; extensions depend on the features usedPHP 8.3+ and documented required extensionsPHP 8.2+ in the current guide; PHP 8.5 requires CodeIgniter 4.7.0+
    InstallationCopy/clone the source, configure .env, and run the native CLI; no ComposerStandard installation uses Composer and the Laravel installer or project creation workflowComposer installation or an officially documented manual ZIP installation
    Class loadingExplicit require_once and registration; no autoloaderComposer-based autoloading and framework conventionsBuilt-in PSR-4 autoloader, with optional Composer integration
    Frontend toolingLocal CSS/JS and server-rendered views; no Node build requiredDocumented frontend workflow uses Vite with Node/npm or Bun; a PHP-only API does not inherently need an asset buildPHP views do not inherently need a Node build; frontend tooling is the application's choice
    CLIphp osoni: generators, migrations, seeds, diagnostics, mail tasks, and explicitly registered custom commandsphp artisan: framework commands, generators, migrations, queue workers, and custom commandsphp spark: framework commands, generators, migrations, and custom commands
    TemplatesPlain PHP or compiled Osoni templates, with escaped {{ ... }} outputBlade templates, with directives, layouts, and componentsPHP views and an optional View Parser
    Data accessPDO query builder plus optional models, casts, and explicit relationships; SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL ServerQuery builder and Eloquent ORM, including relationships, scopes, events, and soft deletesQuery Builder, table-oriented Model classes, and entities; not the same relationship-oriented model API as Eloquent

    Composer is a PHP dependency manager; PSR-4 is a convention for finding classes automatically. Avoiding them reduces Osoni's installation tooling, but means you load files yourself and cannot assume Composer packages will work without adaptation. Conversely, autoloading and package management can reduce repetitive wiring as an application grows. CodeIgniter's manual installation does not disable its autoloader. Osoni templates are a Osoni feature, not Laravel's similarly named authentication scaffolding.

    Application features and operations

    AreaOsoniLaravel 13.xCodeIgniter 4
    AuthenticationIncluded registration/login, verification, password reset, optional authenticator MFA, database-backed bearer tokens and role guards; application-specific role assignment and record ownership remain your responsibilityCore authentication facilities; starter kits provide ready-made UI flows, with additional first-party packages for other authentication needsOfficial Shield package provides authentication and authorization, including access tokens, roles, and permissions; it is separate from the core
    SessionsNative PHP storage or opt-in database sessions; Redis/Memcached cache support does not add session driversIncludes file, database, cookie, Redis, Memcached, DynamoDB, and nonpersistent array drivers, subject to prerequisitesIncludes file, database, Redis, and Memcached session handlers, subject to driver prerequisites
    Shared cacheNative Redis or Memcached extensions; intentionally limited cache APIMultiple cache backends and a broader framework cache APIBuilt-in cache component with multiple handlers, including file, Redis, and Memcached
    Background workNative scheduler and database-backed general-purpose queue with explicit job registries, retries and uncertain-work recovery; separate outgoing-email queueGeneral-purpose job queues, workers, retries, job chaining/batching, and task schedulingGeneral-purpose Queue and Tasks scheduler are available as separate official packages
    File storageApplication-owned local, native SSH2 SFTP, signed S3-compatible and Azure Blob drivers; bounded string API, no automatic credential discoveryFilesystem abstraction with local/cloud adapters and broader streaming/file APIs, subject to packages and configurationFile handling utilities; remote/cloud integration depends on chosen libraries or packages
    Structured importsNative CSV/JSON/XML readers and ext-yaml YAML/YML; eager Data filter/map/transform/validate/export pipeline with explicit DTO factoriesCollections, validation and filesystem tools can compose imports; format-specific parsing depends on selected librariesValidation and data/file tools can compose imports; format-specific parsing depends on selected libraries
    Extension modelEdit explicit PHP services and registries; third-party PHP packages are not part of the framework's dependency modelComposer packages, first-party integrations, and framework extension pointsFramework libraries/modules, Composer integration, and optional official packages
    Deployment scopeSupplied domain-root templates for Apache, Nginx, FrankenPHP standard mode, and IIS; not subdirectory hosting or persistent FrankenPHP workersPublic-directory deployments; official documentation includes Nginx and FrankenPHP, with additional deployment tooling availablePublic-directory application structure; configure the chosen supported PHP/web-server environment
    Release and maintenance planningNo release version or formal support window is currently declared; assess maintenance capacity before adoptingPublished versioning and support policy: framework bug fixes for 18 months and security fixes for two yearsCurrent requirements guide states that only the latest framework version is maintained; review upgrade notes and package compatibility

    The Osoni deployment templates are not a certification of every server configuration. Apache, Nginx, and FrankenPHP have been exercised in the project's Linux integration work; live IIS validation was not performed in that environment. Test your actual operating system, PHP build, database, and server configuration before deployment.

    Which should you choose?

    • Consider Osoni when avoiding Composer and implicit class loading is an explicit requirement, or when you want to follow a request through directly loaded PHP files. Accept the narrower integration model and responsibility for assessing maintenance and production requirements.
    • Consider Laravel when you need Eloquent's broader data model, general-purpose background jobs, first-party integrations, or a package-oriented workflow. Budget learning time for its conventions, service container, and the particular packages your application uses.
    • Consider CodeIgniter when you want an MVC framework with a supported manual-install option and PSR-4 class loading, adding official packages such as Shield, Queue, or Tasks as needed.

    These are fit recommendations, not measured learning-difficulty rankings. A beginner may prefer explicit wiring, or may learn faster with conventions and existing tutorials. Build the same small feature in each candidate before committing: include validation, login, a database change, tests, and deployment, rather than comparing only a “Hello world” page.

    No performance or security winner is claimed. This project has not published a reproducible cross-framework benchmark, independent comparative security audit, or equivalent production load test. Fewer dependencies do not automatically mean greater security; more features do not automatically mean slower applications. All three still require supported runtimes, updates, correct authorization, secure configuration, and operational care. Package availability also does not establish community size, support quality, or a service-level guarantee.

    Official sources and how to verify the comparison

    Osoni's entries describe this repository; follow the installation, sessions, ORM, mail, and production boundaries chapters for implementation details and limitations.

    • Laravel: installation, PHP requirements and deployment, Blade, Eloquent, authentication, sessions, cache, queues, scheduling, and release/support policy.
    • CodeIgniter: requirements, manual installation, autoloading, Spark commands, models, View Parser, sessions, cache, and official packages, including Shield, Queue, and Tasks.

    External sources need an internet connection; the comparison itself remains available in the offline manual. Recheck these sources when upgrading instead of treating this dated comparison as a permanent feature matrix.

    License

    Osoni is licensed under the MIT License. Vendored Swagger UI and its bundled dependencies retain their own licenses and notices under public/assets/swagger-ui/; the framework's MIT license does not replace those third-party terms.

    Language Convention

    All framework-maintained UI, CLI output, diagnostics, emails, generated code, comments, tests, and documentation use US English. The main web layout and Swagger UI declare lang="en-US". CLI examples use page='New page' as the default page. Standard messages include Check your input., This field is required., Use at least 2 characters., and Something went wrong. Please try again later. The reset and verification email subjects are Reset your password and Verify your email address. The example greeting is Hello, Ada!. The CAPTCHA refresh action is Show another code, with the success message New code loaded. Enter the code and submit the form again.

    Applications may explicitly format user data in other locales with the formatter described below; this does not translate framework-maintained copy.

    Getting Started

    If this is your first framework, follow Start Here and the Detailed Installation Guide instead of trying to configure every feature listed below.

    Requirements: PHP 8.3+, PDO, pdo_sqlite for SQLite, pdo_mysql for MySQL, pdo_pgsql with libpq for PostgreSQL, or pdo_sqlsrv plus Microsoft's ODBC Driver for SQL Server, and the standard session, json, and filter extensions. The tests also use native process and socket functions. The CLI uses proc_open for the development server and tests; this function must be available for those tasks. Encryption requires the native openssl extension with AES-256-GCM support. Excel and Word creation require the native zip extension; PDF creation requires iconv. The document tests also use the native dom extension. Localized formatting requires the native intl extension and its ICU data. Upload validation requires native fileinfo; DOCX/XLSX upload checks also require native zip. PHP file uploads must be enabled. AI requests require native curl with HTTPS support and a trusted CA store. Optional shared caching requires native redis (PhpRedis 6+) or memcached (3+) and a running server. No Composer packages are required.

    Terminal
    php osoni init
php osoni storage:prepare
php osoni migrate
php osoni serve

    This is the short version for developers who already have a compatible PHP installation. init creates configuration, storage:prepare creates private working folders, migrate prepares database tables, and serve starts the local website. The detailed guide explains each step and key setup. Seeding example data and running the test suite are optional checks, not requirements for opening the home page.

    Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The example form demonstrates CSRF, validation, and safe HTML output. The development server stays on localhost. Use php osoni serve 8080 for a different port. The home/test page has a responsive light design with local CSS in public/assets/css/welcome.css, a test form with error and success messages, and expandable CLI examples. No external fonts or scripts are loaded.

    init creates a local .env, but never overwrites an existing one. The default is SQLite in database/app.sqlite; the database is created by the first database command. The form does not need a database.

    Detailed Installation Guide

    1. Choose your installation

    Your first visit: complete steps 1, 2 or 3, and 4 through 7. Step 8 covers optional features; step 9 is for deploying a live site later. If PHP is already installed, check its version and extensions before skipping to step 4.

    For the simplest local setup, use PHP 8.3 or later with SQLite and the built-in development server. You do not need Apache, Nginx, IIS, Redis, Composer, npm, or an external database server to try Osoni.

    For production, choose Apache with FastCGI/PHP-FPM, Nginx with PHP-FPM, FrankenPHP standard mode, or IIS FastCGI. Follow the Web Server Deployment chapter after completing the common setup below. Subdirectory hosting and persistent FrankenPHP workers are outside the supplied deployment scope.

    Use a new empty directory for a fresh installation. These instructions are not an upgrade procedure: do not overwrite an existing application's .env, encryption key, database, uploads, or private storage.

    2. Install PHP on Linux

    On a Debian/Ubuntu installation whose configured repositories provide PHP 8.3 or later, the following installs the usual local-development requirements:

    Terminal
    sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install php-cli php-sqlite3 php-intl php-mbstring php-xml php-zip php-curl
php -v
php --ini
php -m
