    Confirm the reported PHP version is at least 8.3. Distribution defaults vary: if your repositories provide an older release, use a supported distribution/repository that provides a compatible PHP version. Do not mix extension packages from different PHP release series.

    Some PHP builds bundle OpenSSL, iconv, JSON, session, filter, and fileinfo; others package them separately. Verify actual modules rather than assuming the package command is sufficient. On other Linux distributions, install equivalent packages through that distribution's supported package manager. For FPM deployment, additionally install the matching php-fpm package (often versioned, such as php8.3-fpm) and configure it with your server. The development server needs only CLI PHP.

    Check the extensions used by the bundled features and native tests:

    Terminal
    php -r 'foreach (["PDO","pdo_sqlite","openssl","session","json","filter","intl","mbstring","fileinfo","curl","iconv","zip","dom"] as $e) { echo $e, ": ", extension_loaded($e) ? "OK" : "MISSING", PHP_EOL; }'

    Install/enable any missing extension for the PHP binary shown by php -v. The native test runner also needs proc_open and local socket functions. If a hosting policy disables them, run the tests on an appropriate development/CI machine; do not blindly weaken a production hosting policy.

    3. Install PHP on Windows

    1. Download a supported PHP 8.3+ Windows ZIP build from https://windows.php.net/download/. Use the architecture matching your system and server. An NTS build is appropriate for CLI development and IIS/FastCGI; Apache module installations require the matching TS/module combination instead. Follow the PHP build's Visual C++ runtime requirements.
    2. Extract PHP to a directory such as C:\PHP. Copy php.ini-development to php.ini for local work; use a reviewed production configuration for deployed services.
    3. Set extension_dir = "C:/PHP/ext" in that INI file. Enable the available extension lines below by removing their leading semicolon:
    Configuration
    extension=pdo_sqlite
extension=sqlite3
extension=openssl
extension=intl
extension=mbstring
extension=fileinfo
extension=curl
extension=zip

    DOM, iconv, JSON, session, filter, and PDO may already be compiled into your build. Verify with php -m; do not add DLL lines for extensions already built in or install DLLs from an incompatible PHP version, architecture, or thread-safety build.

    1. Add C:\PHP to your user/system PATH using Windows Environment Variables, then open a new PowerShell or Command Prompt window.
    2. In PowerShell, verify the executable and loaded configuration:
    PowerShell
    Get-Command php
php -v
php --ini
php -m

    If PHP is not on PATH, run & "C:\PHP\php.exe" -v and use the same explicit executable for the remaining commands. Resolve startup warnings such as “Unable to load dynamic library” before proceeding. No WSL, Bash, or executable permission on the osoni file is required.

    4. Obtain the framework files

    Download and extract the project's source archive, or clone the actual repository URL supplied by your project maintainer. Osoni does not require composer install, autoload generation, or an npm build.

    Use a private working directory such as ~/projects/osoni on Linux or C:\Projects\Osoni on Windows. Do not extract the project directly into a public web root. The full source must include osoni, bootstrap.php, .env.example, framework/, app/, config/, routes/, database/, and public/; enable “show hidden files” when checking archive contents.

    Open a terminal inside the project directory:

    Terminal
    cd /absolute/path/to/osoni
php osoni help

    PowerShell equivalent:

    PowerShell
    Set-Location "C:\Projects\Osoni"
php osoni help

    If your source directory has spaces, quote the path. Do not point commands at another installed copy accidentally. Existing process environment variables override .env; unexpected settings may come from your shell or service definition.

    5. Initialize local configuration

    Terminal
    php osoni init

    This copies .env.example only when .env does not already exist. Open the new .env privately in your editor. For the SQLite/local-development path, verify these values:

    Configuration
    APP_ENV=local
APP_DEBUG=false
APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000
SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=false
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_DATABASE=database/app.sqlite
STORAGE_PATH=storage
CACHE_DRIVER=none

    Leave cache, AI, SMTP, and IMAP credentials empty until you intentionally configure those services. The environment file supports NAME=value, optional matching quotes, and full-line comments; it does not expand shell variables or support inline comments. Keep it out of version control and never paste its contents into tickets or public logs.

    Generate an encryption key:

    Terminal
    php osoni key:generate

    Copy the printed APP_KEY=base64:... assignment into your private .env. The command prints only and does not update the file. Do not publish the output. Keep a separate protected backup; replacing the key later does not re-encrypt existing records and can make encrypted data unrecoverable. On an existing application, preserve its original key.

    6. Prepare storage and the database

    For a fresh local SQLite installation:

    Terminal
    php osoni storage:prepare
php osoni migrate
php osoni migrate:status
php osoni db:seed

    Run one command at a time. The last command, db:seed, is optional. If a command reports an error, resolve it before moving on.

    storage:prepare creates private logs, uploads, and compiled-view directories, plus files when local file storage is selected. migrate creates/applies the bundled schema in the configured SQLite file. migrate:status should show applied batch numbers rather than OPEN. The optional default seeder adds a welcome note; it does not create an administrator or a preconfigured login.

    Run these commands as the identity that should own local application data. On Linux, newly created private files may be readable only by their owner. On Windows, configure NTFS ACLs explicitly; chmod is not equivalent. Do not solve permission errors with chmod 777, administrator-owned application data, or write access to the entire deployed source tree.

    For another database, configure it before migrating:

    DatabaseInstall/prepareRequired environment changes
    SQLiteNative pdo_sqlite; writable local database directoryDB_CONNECTION=sqlite, file path in DB_DATABASE
    MySQLNative pdo_mysql; create an empty database and dedicated accountDB_CONNECTION=mysql, host/port/database/username/password; optional DB_MYSQL_TLS (default disabled)
    PostgreSQLNative pdo_pgsql and libpq; create a database and dedicated accountDB_CONNECTION=pgsql, DB_PORT=5432, connection credentials, DB_SSLMODE=verify-full, CA configuration as required
    SQL ServerNative pdo_sqlsrv plus Microsoft's compatible ODBC Driver; create database/loginDB_CONNECTION=sqlsrv, DB_PORT=1433, connection credentials, DB_ENCRYPT=true, DB_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE=false

    Server database names are existing databases, not filesystem paths; Osoni does not provision the database server or create its database/login. Use an account with the schema permissions needed for migrations, then apply your deployment's least-privilege runtime policy. Keep driver, port, and TLS settings consistent. See the PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and production chapters for their detailed requirements.

    MySQL TLS is optional and configured through .env: DB_MYSQL_TLS=disabled (default) passes no SSL/TLS PDO options, required requires encryption, and verify_ca also verifies the server certificate using DB_MYSQL_SSL_CA. Choose the mode appropriate for your deployment; verified TLS is recommended for remote production databases. See MySQL TLS configuration for examples and compatibility details.

    7. Check the installation and start the application

    Terminal
    php osoni about
php osoni env:check
php osoni test
php osoni serve

    about reports CLI runtime/driver information without credentials. env:check inventories environment key names without printing values; empty unused integration settings are expected. The native tests use isolated fixtures, not your configured application database, and send no external email or AI requests. Optional live database/cache/server integration tests are separate and have their own prerequisites.

    serve is different from the other commands: it keeps running and uses that terminal until you stop it. This is normal, not a frozen command. Keep that terminal open and use a second terminal for other commands. The test command is optional for your first visit; when you do run it, check that the final summary reports no failures.

    Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Confirm that the home page and its CSS load. Check http://127.0.0.1:8000/health for liveness and http://127.0.0.1:8000/ready for database/schema/private-storage readiness. Both should return HTTP 200 after successful setup; /ready returns 503 when its dependencies are not ready.

    Stop the development server with Ctrl+C. If port 8000 is occupied, use php osoni serve 8080 and update APP_URL to http://127.0.0.1:8080 before testing links generated by the application. Never use php osoni serve as the production web server.

    8. Enable optional integrations deliberately

    • Authentication emails: configure a real MAIL_FROM and encrypted SMTP host/port/login. Registration verification and password recovery require delivery; a page loading successfully does not prove mail works. Schedule php osoni mail:work 50 using cron or Windows Task Scheduler. Test delivery only to an authorized address; IMAP is optional.
    • Redis/Memcached: install the selected native extension in CLI and web PHP, configure a protected server and a unique CACHE_PREFIX, then run php osoni cache:test. This deliberately writes/reads/deletes one temporary key. Keep CACHE_DRIVER=none when no cache is configured.
    • OpenAI/Claude: configure the selected provider's API key and exact model ID, plus native cURL/system trust. API usage can incur charges; framework tests do not make real provider requests.
    • Document generation/uploads: verify ZIP, DOM, iconv, fileinfo, PHP upload limits, and writable private storage. Application upload limits cannot raise PHP or web-server limits.
    • Structured file reading: JSON and CSV need no extra extension. XML requires DOM; YAML/YML requires the native PHP YAML extension with yaml.decode_php=0. See Structured File Reading.

    Refer to each integration's chapter before enabling it in production.

    9. Move to a production web server

    1. Back up the database, private data, and encryption key. Configure a real HTTPS origin, production credentials, and stable private storage outside public/; keep its real path free of symlink ancestors.
    2. Set APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, and the HTTPS APP_URL. Set secure cookies and configure actual HTTPS at the server/trusted edge. Restrict public API docs if not intended for public access.
    3. Follow the Apache, Nginx, FrankenPHP, or IIS instructions in Web Server Deployment. Expose **only public/**. Configure the actual web PHP INI/extensions, service identity, sessions, upload temporary directory, timeouts, certificates, and permissions.
    4. Under the deployment identity, run php osoni storage:prepare and review php osoni migrate:status. After a verified backup and schema review, production migration execution requires php osoni migrate --force. Do not automatically run development seeders against production.
    5. Run php osoni doctor. Resolve failures and review every warning. A local installation normally fails production-only checks; that is not evidence that local development is broken.
    6. Smoke-test real HTTPS routes, assets, sessions/login, authorized API requests, uploads, mail delivery, /health, and /ready. Test backups, restores, monitoring, scheduled mail, and expected load before release.

    CLI checks do not certify another PHP SAPI or a complete deployment. The production and server chapters explain remaining operational boundaries.

    Installation troubleshooting

    SymptomCheck and recovery
    php is not recognized / command not foundInstall PHP, correct PATH, open a new terminal, or use the full executable path. Check which PHP binary is running.
    Could not open input file: osoniChange to the project root containing the osoni file, or supply its absolute path.
    PHP startup/DLL warningUse extension binaries/packages matching the PHP version, architecture, and TS/NTS mode; verify extension_dir, dependent runtimes, and php --ini.
    Missing Intl/mbstring/fileinfo/PDO driverEnable/install the extension for the exact CLI/web runtime reporting the error, then restart the relevant service.
    APP_ENV must be ... / invalid typed settingCorrect the named setting in private configuration; inspect process/service overrides. Commands require a successful bootstrap.
    Encryption fails or key is invalidGenerate a valid key for a new installation; restore the original key for existing encrypted data rather than replacing it.
    SQLite cannot open the database / permission deniedCheck the configured absolute/root-relative path and service identity; grant only required directory/file access and keep SQLite on local storage.
    MySQL TLS/CA failureSupply a readable trusted CA and a certificate matching DB_HOST; verify server TLS. Plaintext opt-out is local-development-only.
    /ready returns 503Prepare private storage, check database connectivity/TLS, and apply reviewed pending migrations; inspect private application/PHP logs.
    Home page loads but other routes return server 404Correct the public document root and install/enable the server's supplied rewrite/FastCGI configuration.
    PHP source appears as text/downloadStop public access immediately and configure the PHP handler correctly. Never expose source files as static downloads.
    Cookies/login fail or forms return 419Use a consistent hostname/scheme, writable session storage, and matching secure-cookie settings. Submit the current CSRF token from the same session.
    Verification/reset emails stay queuedConfigure real encrypted SMTP, a valid sender, and scheduled mail:work; check delivery diagnostics without exposing message contents.
    Local doctor returns exit 1It evaluates production deployment. Review each result; do not enable production settings blindly just to make a local check green.

    Windows and Linux

    Use the same commands on both systems with php osoni .... On Windows, this works from PowerShell or cmd, without WSL, Bash, or an executable shebang. Make sure PHP CLI is in PATH; check with php -v and use php --ini to find the configuration file in use. PHP for your web server may use a different configuration file.

    On Windows, enable the required extensions in php.ini: pdo_sqlite for SQLite, pdo_mysql for MySQL, pdo_pgsql for PostgreSQL, or pdo_sqlsrv for SQL Server, and also openssl and iconv for email. Enable zip for Excel/Word creation and dom for the document tests. Enable intl for localized date/time and number formatting. Enable fileinfo for upload validation. Use the correct DLLs for your PHP distribution. OpenSSL requires a valid CA bundle; set openssl.cafile if needed or use the separate SMTP_CA_FILE/IMAP_CA_FILE settings. Do not disable certificate verification.

    Relative database paths are always relative to the project root. Both database/app.sqlite and database\app.sqlite are allowed. Full Windows drive paths and UNC paths are recognized, for example:

    DOTENV
    DB_DATABASE="C:/Data/Osoni/app.sqlite"

    Backslashes are also allowed and are not treated as .env escapes. Do not use drive-relative paths such as C:app.sqlite. UNC paths are recognized as absolute, but use local storage for SQLite: SMB/NFS file locking is not a substitute for a database server. Use MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server for shared databases.

    The CLI starts PHP without a shell, so spaces, percent signs, and other shell characters in project paths are preserved. Generators reject Windows device names such as CON, NUL, and COM1 on both systems. Also keep the exact capitalization of files and require_once paths consistent: Linux is generally case-sensitive, Windows generally is not.

    Linux uses POSIX file permissions: new .env and SQLite files get 0600. Windows uses existing/inherited NTFS ACLs; chmod(0600) does not provide comparable protection there. Therefore, before initialization, use Windows folder security to restrict access to the project folder, data folder, and their backups to the administrator and PHP service user. Give the service user write access only where needed. On Windows, tests check read/write access, not Unix permission bits.

    For local development, php osoni serve works on both systems. Deployment templates and integration tests cover Apache, Nginx, FrankenPHP standard request mode, and IIS FastCGI. Always set the document root to public/; see Web Server Deployment for exact requirements, configuration, and validation boundaries.

    For scheduled email delivery, use cron on Linux and Task Scheduler on Windows. Choose the full path to php/php.exe as the program, provide the absolute path to osoni and mail:work 50 as arguments, and set the project folder as the working directory. Put paths containing spaces in quotes.

    The .github/workflows/tests.yml workflow runs the full native suite on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest, with PHP 8.3 and 8.5, once the project is on GitHub and Actions is enabled. Adding a workflow does not mean a Windows test has been run.

    How a Request Flows

    1. The web server serves only public/.
    2. public/index.php loads bootstrap.php.
    3. The bootstrap explicitly loads the framework files and reads the configuration.
    4. The application loads routes/web.php and the explicit API modules in routes/api.php.
    5. Web requests start a session and check unsafe methods for CSRF. /api and /api/* use a separate stateless router without sessions or cookie authentication.
    6. The router calls your controller, which returns a Response.
    Plain text
    app/
  controllers/       HTTP actions
  models/            ORM models or custom database logic
  views/             PHP views and compiled .osoni.php templates
    layouts/         Shared page structure
    partials/        Reusable page fragments
    components/      Components with props and slots
config/app.php       Typed application settings in use
database/
  migrations/        Anonymous Migration objects with up/down
  seeders/           Closures for example or initial data
framework/           Small native building blocks
public/              Only public document root
routes/web.php       Explicit imports and route registration
routes/api.php       Explicit API module imports (also updated by CLI)
routes/api/          API routes and OpenAPI metadata in the same definition
storage/             Private logs/uploads/views/files and migration lock
tests/run.php        Native tests, including real HTTP requests
bootstrap.php        Explicit framework registration
osoni               CLI, run with php osoni

    CLI Utilities and Custom Commands

    Terminal
    php osoni about
php osoni env:check
php osoni cache:test
php osoni logs:tail
php osoni logs:tail 100 warning
php osoni make:command Report

    Runtime and environment diagnostics

    about prints safe runtime metadata: PHP version, OS family, SAPI, environment, configured database/cache driver names, session handler, and loaded extensions. The framework has no declared release version yet, so the command says so instead of inventing one. It does not print credentials, application keys, connection strings, or filesystem paths, and does not connect to services or create storage. CLI information does not certify the web server's PHP extensions or configuration.

    env:check compares your local .env key names against .env.example, honoring process environment overrides without changing files or loaded configuration. Output contains names and statuses only, never values:

    StatusMeaning
    SETAn effective value is present and nonempty
    EMPTYExplicitly empty; may be intentional for unused integrations
    MISSINGAn active example setting has no file/process value
    OPTIONALA commented example setting has no override
    CUSTOMA local file key is not listed in the example

    Exit code is 1 if active example keys are missing, otherwise 0. Missing keys can still have framework defaults; this is a configuration inventory check, not a production certification. Empty, optional, and custom entries need human review, not automatic replacement. Duplicate/malformed local entries fail explicitly without printing their contents. All CLI commands still require bootstrap to succeed: invalid typed configuration can prevent this command from starting. Use doctor for production settings/readiness.

    Testing cache connectivity

    cache:test checks the selected configured backend using one cryptographically random key in its existing namespace. It writes with a 30-second TTL, verifies the round trip, and deletes only its probe key. It never flushes the server or changes other application keys. Disabled/missing/unreachable backends fail explicitly; there is no fallback. Cleanup is attempted after a successful write; interrupted or uncertain writes expire automatically. Success output contains no key, value, host, or credentials. Native backend failures use the cache service's redacted errors and normal CLI error logging.

    Reading recent application logs

    logs:tail [lines] [level] is a one-shot snapshot, not a continuous watcher. It prints the most recent matching entries in chronological order, across the configured storage directory's daily JSONL files. The line count is 1..1000, default 50. The optional second argument is the minimum severity: debug, info, notice, warning, error, critical, alert, or emergency; default debug includes every level.

    Reading does not create storage, write log files, or trigger retention. Missing logs produce a clear informational message. Symlinked paths, corrupt JSON/levels, entries above 64 KiB, and scans exceeding 8 MiB fail explicitly; request fewer lines or a less restrictive filter for large logs. JSON output escapes terminal control characters. Existing log messages and context may still contain private application data: logger key-based redaction does not sanitize arbitrary message text. Restrict terminal/log access and never paste confidential output into public systems.

    Creating application-specific commands

    make:command Report creates app/commands/Report.php containing a Closure. The generated command deliberately throws until implemented, preventing an empty success-shaped scaffold. Existing files are never overwritten. Implement it, then register it explicitly in routes/console.php:

    PHP
    <?php
declare(strict_types=1);

return [
    'app:report' => require $app->root . '/app/commands/Report.php',
];

    For example, the command file can return:

    PHP
    <?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Osoni\Application;

return static function (Application $app, array $arguments): int {
    if ($arguments !== []) {
        throw new InvalidArgumentException('Usage: php osoni app:report');
    }
    echo "Report completed.\n";
    return 0;
};

    Run php osoni app:report. Help lists registered custom names. The registry is optional for older projects; create it with the structure above. There is no Composer, autoloading, or command-directory scanning. Names must match lowercase letter-led segments containing letters, digits, or hyphens, optionally separated by colons. Builtin names cannot be overridden; every entry must be a Closure.

    Handlers receive the Application and unchanged remaining CLI arguments, including any options. They must validate their arguments themselves and return an integer exit code from 0 through 255. Exceptions use the existing CLI error path. Custom commands must implement their own production guards, authorization, confirmation, and secret handling; builtin --force safeguards do not automatically apply to arbitrary custom code. The five utility commands above do not accept --force or other options.

    Web Server Deployment

    Osoni uses ordinary PHP requests, REQUEST_URI, standard HTTP headers, and explicit bootstrap files; it does not depend on Apache-specific APIs. The deployment scope is a domain root, not a subdirectory/virtual directory. FrankenPHP is configured in standard request mode, not persistent worker mode. Do not enable workers without implementing and testing a separate request-state lifecycle.

    ServerSupplied configurationPHP integration
    Apache 2.4+deploy/apache.conf and public/.htaccessPHP-FPM/FastCGI example; an administrator can use an equivalent mod_php setup
    Nginxdeploy/nginx.confPHP-FPM/FastCGI, only /index.php
    FrankenPHPdeploy/CaddyfileEmbedded PHP in standard request mode
    IIS 10+ on Windowspublic/web.configPHP NTS through FastCGI, with Microsoft URL Rewrite 2.x

    These are supported deployment paths, not a promise that every upstream server version, module combination, OS build, proxy, or hosting policy will work without configuration. The framework remains Windows/Linux portable; server availability and production suitability follow each upstream project. In particular, IIS is Windows-only, and FrankenPHP builds/extensions must support your selected platform; do not assume native Windows FrankenPHP or production-grade Windows Nginx support from framework portability alone.

    Shared deployment contract

    1. The document root/physical site path must be **only public/**. Never expose the project root, even if a rewrite rule appears to hide it.
    2. index.php is the only public PHP entry point. The templates block direct access to other PHP/PHAR/PHTML scripts, including the development router. Existing directories must not bypass routing or expose directory listings.
    3. Only existing CSS, JS, PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/ICO/SVG, and WOFF/WOFF2 files are served directly. Other paths go to the framework; hidden paths and common secret/database/log/config/backup extensions are denied. This intentionally tightens the previous Apache behavior that served any existing public file. If your application needs another static type, update and test all deployed server allowlists and the development router deliberately.
    4. Preserve the original URI/query string, method, raw request body, Authorization header, status code, response body, and Allow header. Do not replace framework JSON 4xx/5xx errors with HTML error pages.
    5. Install the same required PHP extensions in the web runtime as in CLI. FrankenPHP has its own embedded PHP/extensions/INI configuration; a successful php -m for CLI does not prove its extensions are available.
    6. Configure writable private storage, persistent SQLite/database access, PHP session storage, and upload temporary storage for the actual service identity. Keep application source read-only. Run storage:prepare and migrations with a compatible deployment identity; run php osoni doctor.
    7. Terminate HTTPS at the server or a trusted edge. Set APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, and the real HTTPS APP_URL. Set SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true behind TLS termination; the flag does not encrypt HTTP or validate proxy identity. Never trust arbitrary forwarded headers. Restore client IPs only using an allowlisted proxy configuration.

    The templates permit an 8 MiB server request body. Configure PHP post_max_size=8M, upload_max_filesize=3M (or values appropriate to your application), a writable upload_tmp_dir, and persistent session.save_path. The framework still enforces its independent 1 MiB JSON/API request limit and default 2 MiB per-file upload limit. Native server/PHP limits can reject a request before PHP runs; those responses may be server-generated, not JSON. Coordinate execution/FastCGI/proxy timeouts with long AI operations, and disable response buffering where your application requires streaming. Server-side URLs with encoded slashes, double escaping, or invalid characters may be rejected earlier by different servers; do not loosen these protections to make malformed requests behave identically.

    Apache

    Start from deploy/apache.conf. Replace the hostname, /srv/osoni/public, and PHP-FPM socket. Enable mod_rewrite, mod_proxy, and mod_proxy_fcgi, with the usual authorization, directory, and MIME modules. Permit the included .htaccess overrides for this trusted application directory, or move those rules into the equivalent directory configuration if your host disables overrides. Apache must be 2.4+ because the rewrite rules use END.

    The template's CGIPassAuth On plus rewrite authorization mapping preserves bearer tokens through FastCGI/internal rewrites. The PHP handler is scoped to index.php; do not add a generic executable-files directory. For Windows Apache/FastCGI, use forward-slash paths such as C:/Sites/Osoni/public and replace the handler endpoint with, for example, proxy:fcgi://127.0.0.1:9000. Install and supervise a compatible FastCGI process manager; PHP-FPM itself is not a native Windows service. For mod_php, have your administrator replace the FPM handler with the installed module's PHP handler and appropriate MPM/thread-safety combination; keep the rewrite and access restrictions.

    Validate with apachectl configtest (or httpd.exe -t), then reload through your service manager. Add actual TLS certificates/bindings and HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection; the supplied port-80 virtual host alone is not a production TLS configuration.

    Nginx

    Include deploy/nginx.conf inside the http block. Replace the hostname, public path, and FPM socket; for a separately managed FastCGI service, a TCP endpoint such as 127.0.0.1:9000 can be used instead. Include your distribution's fastcgi_params, which must preserve QUERY_STRING, REQUEST_METHOD, CONTENT_TYPE, CONTENT_LENGTH, REQUEST_URI, REMOTE_ADDR, and HTTPS where applicable.

    The template explicitly sets SCRIPT_FILENAME to the front controller and forwards HTTP_AUTHORIZATION. It does not use $uri/ directory fallbacks that bypass the router. Do not add a second broad PHP execution location. The location explicitly sets fastcgi_intercept_errors off; settings that replace application errors break API error behavior. Run nginx -t, configure TLS/listen directives and certificates, and reload through your service manager. Restrict any TCP FastCGI listener to trusted local/server networks.

    FrankenPHP

    Use the Caddyfile with a FrankenPHP build containing PHP 8.3+ and all required extensions. It is not a configuration for plain Caddy: the frankenphp/php directives require FrankenPHP.

    For local HTTP validation on Linux:

    Terminal
    OSONI_PUBLIC_ROOT=/absolute/path/to/osoni/public \
OSONI_SERVER_NAME=http://127.0.0.1:8080 \
frankenphp run --config deploy/Caddyfile

    In production, set OSONI_PUBLIC_ROOT to the real public directory and OSONI_SERVER_NAME to your public domain, for example app.example.com. Caddy automatic HTTPS requires working DNS, reachable ports, permissions, and persistent certificate/configuration storage. Configure service environment variables rather than relying on an interactive shell. These two deployment variables are read by Caddy before PHP starts; putting them only in Osoni's .env does not configure Caddy.

    Run frankenphp validate --config deploy/Caddyfile under the same service environment, then run/supervise it normally. The configuration preserves the original URI while internally executing only the front controller. It intentionally does not configure workers, an FPM backend, or directory indexes. Configure the Caddy administration endpoint appropriately and persist its HTTPS data when using containers.

    IIS

    Install IIS 10+ with the CGI/FastCGI feature, Microsoft URL Rewrite 2.x, and a PHP 8.3+ NTS build matching the server architecture. Point the site's physical path to C:\Sites\Osoni\public, not the project root. The supplied web.config provides rewrite rules, hidden file protection, static-file routing, disabled directory browsing, a default document, the request-body cap, and httpErrors existingResponse=PassThrough. IIS does not read .htaccess.

    In IIS Manager (administrator):

    1. Create a dedicated application pool with No Managed Code and a compatible bitness, using a least-privilege application-pool identity.
    2. Add a FastCGI application pointing to the actual php-cgi.exe. Set PHPRC to your PHP configuration directory and align PHP_FCGI_MAX_REQUESTS with the FastCGI instanceMaxRequests setting.
    3. Add a handler mapping for index.php, verbs *, module FastCgiModule, script processor C:\PHP\php-cgi.exe, and file resource type. A generic *.php mapping is unnecessary; remove conflicting inherited handlers. Place the PHP mapping before the catch-all StaticFile handler.
    4. Enable Anonymous Authentication using the application-pool identity (empty anonymous username), so framework sessions/bearer tokens handle application authentication. Disable IIS Windows/Basic authentication unless deliberately integrating it separately.
    5. Remove/disable WebDAV handlers/modules for this site if installed: otherwise they can intercept PUT/DELETE before the framework sees them. Permit required verbs in IIS Request Filtering.
    6. Grant the pool identity read/execute access to source and PHP binaries, and Modify access only to private storage, SQLite's directory/file when used, session storage, and upload temporary storage. Restrict NTFS ACLs; Unix-style chmod is not a Windows access-control substitute.
    7. Configure HTTPS bindings/certificates, request/activity timeouts, and PHP error logging. Do not expose detailed PHP or IIS errors publicly.

    The PHP executable path, machine-level FastCGI registration, and credentials are intentionally not hardcoded in web.config. If IIS reports 500.19, install URL Rewrite and check delegation/locking for the referenced sections with your administrator; do not remove protections just to suppress it. If APIs return server HTML instead of JSON, inspect inherited httpErrors, authentication, WebDAV, and request-filtering settings.

    Real-server compatibility tests

    The common smoke suite exercises actual routing (including UTF-8 paths and query strings), assets/MIME types, private-file denial, single-script execution, bearer-token authentication, POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE JSON, request limits, cookies/CSRF, multipart uploads, readiness/HEAD probes, redirects, and application errors. It creates a new disposable application and database; it never uses the developer's .env, storage, or database.

    On Linux with the matching servers/PHP-FPM installed:

    Terminal
    php tests/web-server-integration.php apache
php tests/web-server-integration.php nginx
php tests/web-server-integration.php frankenphp

    Optional executable overrides are APACHE_BINARY, APACHE_MODULE_DIR, NGINX_BINARY, NGINX_FASTCGI_PARAMS, NGINX_MIME_TYPES, PHP_FPM_BINARY, and FRANKENPHP_BINARY. Apache's Linux harness assumes /etc/mime.types; Nginx defaults to distribution files under /etc/nginx. The harness uses loopback/ephemeral HTTP ports, starts its own child processes without changing running services, and cleans up its own fixtures. Test launcher requirements include native PHP posix, process, and socket functions on Linux.

    On a disposable Windows IIS host, run as administrator in Windows PowerShell with IIS CGI, URL Rewrite, and PHP installed:

    PowerShell
    .\tests\web-server-iis.ps1

    The IIS launcher creates a GUID-named loopback site/application pool, a distinct FastCGI registration, and a disposable database, then removes only its own resources. Do not use a production IIS machine as a test environment.

    CI defines Apache/Nginx/FPM jobs on Linux and IIS jobs on Windows for PHP 8.3/8.5, plus a pinned, checksum-verified FrankenPHP integration job using its embedded PHP runtime. The native suite also validates the IIS XML and request/authorization mapping. A workflow definition is not proof of a successful run: require passing CI and real deployment smoke tests before claiming compatibility for your specific infrastructure. Linux testing cannot certify IIS or Windows-specific extension behavior.

    Redis and Memcached Cache

    The shared $app->cache service supports Redis and Memcached using native PHP extensions, without Composer. It is optional and disabled by default. It does not replace PHP sessions, database-backed rate limits, the mail queue, or the compiled-template cache.

    Enable the matching extension in both CLI and web PHP. For example, on Linux install your PHP distribution's redis or memcached extension package. On Windows, use a compatible extension build matching your PHP version, architecture, and thread-safety mode; enable it in the appropriate php.ini. The modern memcached extension is used, not the legacy memcache extension. Verify with php --ri redis or php --ri memcached. A separate Redis or Memcached server is required; it may run on another private host.

    Cache configuration

    Choose one backend in your private .env:

    Configuration
    CACHE_DRIVER=redis
CACHE_PREFIX=myapp-production:
CACHE_TIMEOUT=2
REDIS_HOST=127.0.0.1
REDIS_PORT=6379
REDIS_DATABASE=0
REDIS_TLS=false

    For Memcached, use CACHE_DRIVER=memcached, MEMCACHED_HOST=127.0.0.1, and MEMCACHED_PORT=11211. Set CACHE_DRIVER=none to disable caching explicitly. Disabled or unavailable caching throws when used: it never pretends that a failed operation is a miss or silently switches to local memory. Construction and normal bootstrap do not connect to either server. There is no application-level automatic retry.

    Use a unique CACHE_PREFIX per application and environment (1..64 ASCII letters, digits, :, _, or -). Keys are stored as the prefix plus a SHA-256 hash, keeping backend keys bounded and separating namespaces. Prefixes and hashes are not authorization or encryption. Never share cache write access with untrusted applications.

    Redis supports password-only authentication with REDIS_PASSWORD, or ACL authentication with both REDIS_USERNAME and REDIS_PASSWORD. Set REDIS_TLS=true for verified TLS; REDIS_CA_FILE optionally selects a trusted CA bundle, otherwise system trust applies. The certificate must match REDIS_HOST; certificate and hostname verification cannot be disabled. Redis ACLs must permit GET, SET, SETEX, DEL, SELECT, EVAL, INCRBY, and EXPIRE. This is a single-server adapter, not a Redis Cluster/Sentinel client.

    Memcached supports optional SASL through MEMCACHED_USERNAME and MEMCACHED_PASSWORD (both required together), with a SASL-capable extension and server. It uses binary protocol. SASL is authentication, not encryption: this adapter does not provide Memcached TLS. Use a protected private network or a separately secured tunnel; never expose Memcached publicly. Plaintext Redis is likewise appropriate only on a trusted network. Do not put credentials in controllers, logs, or version control.

    Cache values, expiration, and remembered results

    PHP
    $app->cache->set('catalog:featured', ['id' => 42, 'name' => 'Notebook'], 600);
$featured = $app->cache->get('catalog:featured', []); // Default only on a miss.
$removed = $app->cache->delete('catalog:featured');  // false if already absent.

$app->cache->set('feature:enabled', false, 60);
$enabled = $app->cache->get('feature:enabled', true); // false, not the default.
$app->cache->set('optional:value', null, 60);        // null is cacheable too.

$notes = $app->cache->remember('notes:recent', function () use ($app): array {
    return $app->db->table('notes')->orderBy('id', 'desc')->limit(10)->get();
}, 120);

    set(), remember(), and increment() default to 300 seconds. TTL is a relative integer number of seconds, 0..31536000 (one year); 0 means no expiration, not deletion. Values may still be evicted by the server. Memcached's special absolute-timestamp behavior above 30 days is normalized automatically. get() defaults to null on a genuine missing/expired key. delete() returns whether an entry was removed and never flushes the server. There is intentionally no whole-server clear operation.

    Values support null, booleans, integers, finite floats, valid UTF-8 strings, and nested arrays. PHP objects (including models and dates), resources, recursive arrays, and invalid UTF-8 are rejected. Convert models to arrays before caching them. JSON encoding is limited to 512 KiB per value and 60 nested array levels; no PHP object serialization is written by this service. Only use trusted cache servers; data retrieved from a cache is not an authorization decision and must still be escaped for HTML output.

    remember() runs the callback only on a miss, including when a previously cached value is null or false. Callback exceptions propagate unchanged and are not cached. Concurrent misses may run the producer more than once: this helper is not a distributed lock or stampede-prevention mechanism. Backend/extension/protocol failures throw RuntimeException, rather than returning a default or calling the producer. Invalid API inputs throw InvalidArgumentException. Native errors are redacted; uncaught exceptions use the framework's existing web/CLI error handling and logging.

    Atomic cache counters

    PHP
    $views = $app->cache->increment('article:42:views', 1, 3600);
$views = $app->cache->increment('article:42:views', 5); // Add five.

    A missing counter starts at the positive amount (default 1). Existing counters must contain nonnegative integers; integer values written by set() can be incremented, but numeric strings cannot. Creation/expiration and increments are atomic. TTL applies only when creating the counter; increments preserve the existing expiry. Redis requires Lua/EVAL permission for this. Keep counters within PHP_INT_MAX. Redis rejects signed-64-bit overflow; Memcached uses native unsigned-64-bit arithmetic, which can wrap at its limit. Values outside PHP's integer range cause an exception, potentially after Memcached has changed the counter. These evictable counters are not durable financial records, distributed locks, or a replacement for the framework's existing authentication/API rate limits.

    Cache deployment checks and tests

    php osoni doctor checks whether the selected native extension is loaded and reminds you to verify server/network settings. It does not connect to or write to cache servers; /ready remains a database/storage/schema check. Test real cache connectivity and application behavior separately in staging.

    The native suite tests validation and optional-extension behavior without requiring servers. Live integration tests use random isolated prefixes and delete only their own keys; they never flush shared servers:

    Terminal
    CACHE_TEST_DRIVER=redis php tests/cache-integration.php
CACHE_TEST_DRIVER=memcached php tests/cache-integration.php

    In PowerShell, set $env:CACHE_TEST_DRIVER = "redis" before running the PHP command. Optional test variables are CACHE_TEST_HOST, CACHE_TEST_PORT, CACHE_TEST_USERNAME, CACHE_TEST_PASSWORD, CACHE_TEST_TLS, and CACHE_TEST_CA_FILE. Use disposable test servers. CI runs both integrations with PHP 8.3 and 8.5.

    AI: Claude and OpenAI

    The server-side $app->ai service supports text conversations and incremental text streaming through OpenAI's Responses API and Anthropic's Claude Messages API. It uses native PHP cURL, not an SDK or Composer. It does not create public routes or a chat UI. ChatGPT/Claude subscriptions do not provide API credentials or include API usage; obtain a provider API key and enable billing/access separately.

    Configuration

    Add these settings to your existing .env or process environment. Set only the providers you use; never commit real API keys:

    DOTENV
    AI_PROVIDER=openai
AI_TIMEOUT=60
AI_MAX_TOKENS=1024
AI_CA_FILE=
OPENAI_API_KEY=
OPENAI_MODEL=
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=

    AI_PROVIDER accepts openai or anthropic (Claude). Set the API key and exact API model ID available to that account, not a ChatGPT/Claude UI label. Model settings are intentionally empty: no possibly retired model is silently chosen. Provider construction makes no network requests and permits unconfigured providers; calling an unconfigured provider fails explicitly.

    AI_TIMEOUT is the complete request deadline in seconds (1..300), including streaming. Connection setup is capped at the smaller of 15 seconds and that deadline. AI_MAX_TOKENS is the default output budget (1..128000); each model may enforce lower limits. Some reasoning models use output tokens internally, leaving fewer visible text tokens. AI_CA_FILE optionally specifies a readable CA bundle; otherwise native cURL/system trust and curl.cainfo apply. Keep certificate verification enabled and configure the correct CA store on both Windows and Linux.

    Bootstrap reads config/ai.php and exposes $app->ai. Programmatic application configuration can supply ai with provider, integer timeout/max_tokens, ca_file, and openai/anthropic arrays containing key and model. API keys and models are validated only for the provider used by each call.

    Text conversations

    PHP
    $app = require __DIR__ . '/bootstrap.php';

$reply = $app->ai->chat(
    [['role' => 'user', 'content' => 'Explain PHP routing in two sentences.']],
    provider: 'anthropic',
    system: 'Be concise and use US English.',
    maxTokens: 512,
);

echo $reply['text']; // Plain-text CLI output. Escape with e() in HTML.

    Omit provider to use AI_PROVIDER. Optional model and maxTokens named arguments override configuration for one call only. system is a separate trusted instruction string, not an entry with role system.

    Pass a nonempty list of messages containing exactly role (user or assistant) and nonempty UTF-8 content. The caller owns conversation history:

    PHP
    $messages = [['role' => 'user', 'content' => 'What is CSRF?']];
$first = $app->ai->chat($messages, provider: 'openai');
$messages[] = ['role' => 'assistant', 'content' => $first['text']];
$messages[] = ['role' => 'user', 'content' => 'Give a short PHP example.'];
$second = $app->ai->chat($messages, provider: 'openai');

    Every successful call returns exactly:

    KeyMeaning
    provideropenai or anthropic
    idProvider response/message ID
    modelModel ID reported by the provider
    textCombined visible text, including an OpenAI text refusal when returned
    finish_reasonExplicit provider completion reason; inspect before treating text as complete
    input_tokensProvider-reported nonnegative input-token counter
    output_tokensProvider-reported nonnegative output-token counter

    OpenAI normally reports completed; text refusals report refusal. A token-budget-limited OpenAI response reports max_output_tokens. Claude normally reports end_turn, with possible max_tokens, stop_sequence, refusal, or model_context_window_exceeded. Token/context-limit results contain partial text: inspect the reason and decide whether to request more. Empty visible text, provider failures, and unsupported non-text results throw rather than returning a success-shaped empty answer. Token counters are not a cost estimate and do not include separately reported cache counters or pricing calculations.

    Streaming text

    PHP
    $reply = $app->ai->stream(
    [['role' => 'user', 'content' => 'Explain prepared statements briefly.']],
    static function (string $delta): void {
        echo $delta; // Plain-text CLI output, not HTML.
    },
    provider: 'openai',
    system: 'Use plain text.',
);

// $reply contains the same metadata and complete assembled text as chat().

    The callback runs synchronously for each nonempty text delta as it arrives, not after the whole response has been buffered. The method returns only after a valid terminal event and complete HTTP transfer. SSE comments, fragmented UTF-8/network chunks, LF/CRLF/CR framing, and multiline data fields are handled. If your callback throws, the connection is canceled and that exception propagates.

    Partial output is not proof of success. An HTTP interruption, timeout, provider stream error, malformed event, missing terminal event, or mismatched OpenAI final text throws even when the callback has already received text. Do not automatically retry streams, and do not persist a partial answer as complete. There are no automatic retries or provider fallback, avoiding duplicate output and unexpected charges.

    This callback API is not an HTTP SSE endpoint. Application code must explicitly authenticate/authorize any endpoint it adds, impose rate limits and spending budgets, choose framing/content types, and configure proxy/output buffering and PHP execution timeouts. Close an active PHP session with session_write_close() before a long-running web stream if it no longer needs session changes.

    Errors, limits, and privacy

    Invalid caller input or missing selected-provider configuration throws InvalidArgumentException. HTTP, network/TLS, provider, JSON, unsupported-content, and premature-stream failures throw RuntimeException. Non-200 HTTP errors include their status in $error->getCode() (for example 401 or 429) but never copy raw provider error bodies or credentials into the exception message. Catch errors at the application boundary and show a generic failure; inspect only safe metadata in private diagnostics. Callback exceptions remain unchanged.

    The native client uses fixed HTTPS provider URLs, verifies TLS certificates and hostnames, never follows redirects, and enforces a total timeout. Requests are capped at 4 MiB; responses at 16 MiB including stream metadata; each SSE event at 4 MiB. Provider token/context limits still apply. The framework does not store or log keys, prompts, responses, or conversation history. OpenAI requests set store=false, which is not a guarantee of zero provider retention: check each provider's data policies before sending personal or confidential content.

    AI output is untrusted. Escape it in HTML, never execute generated code or SQL automatically, and do not let prompts grant authorization. Keep API keys out of browser scripts, templates, logs, and source control. This API supports only text input/output; images, tools/function calls, structured output, audio, provider-side conversation persistence, and full reasoning-state replay are not implemented.

    For isolated tests, new \Osoni\Ai($config, $transport) accepts an optional trusted transport Closure with signature function (string $url, array $headers, string $json, int $timeout, \Closure $receive): void. It must synchronously pass successful response-body chunks to $receive and throw for network errors or non-200 HTTP responses. The replacement controls its own TLS, HTTP status, and timeout safeguards; never derive it from request input. Normal applications should use the built-in transport.

    Provider protocols: OpenAI Responses API, OpenAI streaming, Claude Messages API, Claude streaming.

    HTML Helpers

    Osoni\Html is a lightweight static utility loaded by bootstrap. It builds escaped HTML without an Application service, Composer package, or a new template language. Existing e(), View::escape(), Osoni autoescaping, router, and CSRF behavior remain unchanged.

    PHP
    use Osoni\Html;

echo Html::escape($name);
echo Html::tag('div', 'Hello', [
    'class' => ['container', 'active' => true],
    'data-id' => 123,
    'aria-live' => 'polite',
]);
echo Html::a('/users', 'Users');
echo Html::img('/logo.png', ['alt' => 'Osoni']);

    Escaped text and explicit trusted HTML

    Text and quoted attribute values reuse the existing UTF-8 escaping functions. Quotes, angle brackets, and ampersands are escaped; invalid UTF-8 bytes use replacement characters. Pass unescaped data, not pre-encoded entities. Scalar values, null, and Stringable values are supported; arbitrary objects and arrays are not text.

    Ordinary strings are always text, even if they look like HTML:

    PHP
    echo Html::tag('p', '<strong>Hello</strong>');
// <p>&lt;strong&gt;Hello&lt;/strong&gt;</p>

echo Html::tag('p', Html::raw(Html::tag('strong', $name)));
// One paragraph containing a strong element; $name is still escaped.

    Html::raw() returns an explicit HtmlString trusted-markup wrapper. It is not a sanitizer: never pass user-submitted HTML to it. Only use it for application-authored markup or output composed entirely by these helpers. Plain Stringable objects are not implicitly trusted. Attribute values reject raw HTML; textarea, option, and title content always escape it.

    Helpers return ordinary HTML strings (except raw() and csrf()), so render them intentionally:

    PHP
    <?= \Osoni\Html::a('/users', $label) ?>

    In Osoni, use explicit raw output for the completed helper result:

    HTML
    {!! \Osoni\Html::a('/users', $label) !!}

    Do not use raw output on $label itself. {{ $value }} continues escaping all values, including HtmlString; this feature does not change template trust rules.

    Attributes, classes, and void elements

    PHP
    echo Html::input('text', 'name', [
    'id' => 'name',
    'value' => $name,
    'required' => true,
    'disabled' => false,
    'class' => ['field', 'invalid' => $hasError],
    'data-id' => 123,
    'aria-invalid' => $hasError,
]);

// For an existing application-authored opening tag:
echo '<div' . Html::attributes(['class' => ['panel', 'wide']]) . '>...</div>';

$classes = Html::classes(['panel', ['wide', 'panel'], 'active' => true]);
// "panel wide active" (unescaped tokens; use attributes() when rendering).

    attributes() includes a leading space when nonempty. Names are normalized to lowercase; invalid names and case-insensitive duplicates fail. True native boolean attributes render bare (required), false/null omit them. Boolean attributes require actual booleans, not strings such as "false". For other attributes, booleans become "true"/"false" strings, so ARIA/data state is preserved. The overloaded download/capture attributes accept true for a bare attribute, false to omit, or a string value. Null always omits. data-* and aria-* values are escaped, not automatically JSON-encoded; explicitly use json_encode() for structured data.

    Class arrays accept strings, nested lists, boolean conditional maps, and false/null list entries. Duplicate tokens are removed in first-seen order; nesting is limited to 32. Pass the resulting string through attributes(), not directly into unquoted markup.

    tag() handles uncommon elements without a helper for every tag:

    PHP
    echo Html::tag('section', $heading, ['class' => 'summary']);
echo Html::tag('br'); // <br>, never <br></br>

    Void elements reject content. Element/attribute names are trusted application structure, not arbitrary request parameters. The lightweight API deliberately rejects executable/raw-text and foreign-content elements (including script, style, iframe, SVG, and MathML), custom element names, event handlers, inline styles, srcdoc, srcset, ping, namespace attributes, and customized built-ins. Use reviewed application templates for those specialized contexts. It does not parse or clean HTML, and these checks are not a general sanitization service.

    Links and URL safety

    Links accept local absolute/relative paths, fragments, query strings, and explicit http, https, mailto, or tel URLs. Image sources and other supported URL attributes accept local paths or HTTP(S), not mailto/tel. HTTP(S) URLs require a host and reject embedded credentials.

    PHP
    echo Html::a('/users?' . http_build_query(['search' => $search]), 'Search');
echo Html::a('https://example.test/help', 'Help', [
    'target' => '_blank',
    'rel' => 'noopener noreferrer',
]);

    JavaScript/data/blob/file URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//host), whitespace, controls, and backslashes are rejected. Do not pre-escape URLs; attributes are escaped after checking. Use rawurlencode() for dynamic path segments and http_build_query() for queries. There is no named-route generator in the existing router, so the helper accepts your route path directly.

    External HTTP(S) links are allowed. This is not host authorization, URL reachability checking, SSRF protection, or a replacement for the stricter local-only Response::redirect(). Continue applying your application's allowed destination policy.

    Form controls and CSRF

    PHP
    echo Html::label('email', 'Email address');
echo Html::input('email', 'email', [
    'id' => 'email', 'value' => $email, 'required' => true,
]);
echo Html::textarea('description', $description, ['rows' => 5]);
echo Html::select('status', [
    'active' => 'Active', 'inactive' => 'Inactive',
], 'active');
echo Html::checkbox('active', 1, true, ['id' => 'active']);
echo Html::radio('type', 'admin', false, ['id' => 'type-admin']);
echo Html::button('Save', ['type' => 'submit']);

    Labels reference the control's id, not its name; set matching IDs explicitly. Textarea values are content, never a value attribute. Select options are a flat value => label map; labels always escape, and selections match exact string representations (0 differs from "01"). For multiple selection, set multiple => true, pass a selection array, and use your application's intended array field name:

    PHP
    echo Html::select('roles[]', ['reader' => 'Reader', 'editor' => 'Editor'],
    ['reader'], ['multiple' => true]);

    Checkboxes/radios do not add hidden unchecked fields. Buttons default to type="button" to avoid accidental submission; specify submit explicitly. Attributes cannot override positional arguments such as name, href, or checked; invalid usage throws InvalidArgumentException instead of silently choosing one.

    For browser forms, let the normal application lifecycle start the session, then reuse its existing CSRF protection:

    PHP
    $content = (string) Html::csrf($app->session)
    . Html::input('text', 'name', ['value' => $name])
    . Html::button('Save', ['type' => 'submit']);
echo Html::tag('form', Html::raw($content), [
    'method' => 'post', 'action' => '/users',
]);

    Html::csrf() wraps the existing csrf_field() output; it does not start a session or implement another token system. Existing plain-PHP csrf_field() and Osoni @csrf($session) remain valid alternatives. Merely rendering a form with tag() does not insert a token: explicitly include it for mutations and retain normal server-side CSRF, authentication, authorization, and validation. These are output builders, not a replacement for the Form Generator.

    Form Generator

    Create a standalone Osoni form view using field:type arguments:

    Terminal
    php osoni make:form forms.contact name:text email:email message:textarea

    This writes app/views/forms/contact.osoni.php. Names use the same dot-separated format as other view generators; fields use lowercase snake_case names beginning with a letter. At least one field is required and duplicate fields are rejected. Supported types: text, email, password, textarea, number, date, time, datetime-local, url, tel, and checkbox. Selects and file uploads are not generated; add those controls manually when needed.

    The generated POST form includes @csrf($session), associated labels, and escaped previous values. Field errors use aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Passwords are never repopulated; their autocomplete defaults to new-password (change it to current-password for a login form). Checkboxes submit 1 when checked and submit nothing when unchecked; previous values 1, '1', or true restore the checked state. Array-valued old input is not inserted into controls. Fields are optional by default: add required, lengths, limits, and other HTML attributes to suit your form, and always validate on the server.

    Render the form with a Session and a trusted local action URL. Optional old values are an array keyed by field name; errors has the array<string, list<string>> shape returned by Validator::errors():

    PHP
    // Inside a controller action; register the GET/POST routes explicitly yourself.
$input = $request->method === 'POST' ? $request->all() : [];
$errors = $request->method === 'POST'
    ? \Osoni\Validator::errors($input, [
        'name' => 'required|string|max:80',
        'email' => 'required|email|max:254',
        'message' => 'required|string|max:2000',
    ])
    : [];

// Handle a valid POST here, then redirect; this example only renders the view.
return new \Osoni\Response($this->app->views->render('forms.contact', [
    'session' => $this->app->session,
    'action' => '/contact',
    'old' => array_intersect_key($input, array_flip(['name', 'email', 'message'])),
    'errors' => $errors,
]), $errors === [] ? 200 : 422);

    Only the form markup is generated, not a layout, controller, route, validation rules, authorization, bot protection, or data storage. Include it in a page with @include('forms.contact'), or add your own layout. Include a particular form only once per page so its generated label/error IDs remain unique. Do not retain passwords or other secrets in old, logs, or sessions.

    Existing .php and .osoni.php views are preserved. The command rejects --force rather than overwriting them.

    Controllers and Routes

    Terminal
    php osoni make:controller MessageController
php osoni make:view messages.index
php osoni make:model Message

    Load a new controller explicitly yourself in routes/web.php:

    PHP
    require_once $app->root . '/app/controllers/MessageController.php';

$controller = new \App\Controllers\MessageController($app);
$router->get('/berichten', [$controller, 'index']);

    A controller action receives a Request first, followed by any route parameters in order, and always returns a Response:

    PHP
    $router->get('/berichten/{id}', static function (\Osoni\Request $request, string $id): \Osoni\Response {
    return \Osoni\Response::json(['id' => $id]);
});

$router->post('/berichten', [$controller, 'store']);
$router->add('DELETE', '/berichten/{id}', [$controller, 'destroy']);

    Register specific routes before parameter routes. Parameters cover one path segment; custom regex in routes is intentionally not supported. Trailing slashes are equivalent. HEAD uses GET unless an explicit HEAD route exists. Unknown paths return 404, and incorrect methods return 405 with an Allow header. There is no automatic OPTIONS/CORS or method-override support.

    Read form and JSON input with $request->input('name'), all body fields with $request->all(), and query parameters separately with $request->query('page'). JSON must be an object; invalid JSON returns 400. On web routes, read multipart uploads separately with $request->file('document') or $request->files('documents'). Uploaded files are not included in all().

    PHP
    return new \Osoni\Response($this->app->views->render('messages.index', [
    'title' => 'My messages',
]));

return \Osoni\Response::json(['saved' => true], 201);
return \Osoni\Response::redirect('/berichten');

    Redirects accept only local paths that start with a single /.

    Request and response abstractions

    Controllers receive a Osoni\Request and return a Osoni\Response. Keep direct access to $_GET, $_POST, $_FILES, $_COOKIE, and $_SERVER at the framework's capture boundary:

    PHP
    $name = $request->input('name', '');
$page = $request->query('page', '1');
$authorization = $request->header('Authorization');
$cookie = $request->cookie('session');
$document = $request->file('document'); // UploadedFile|null
$isJson = $request->isJson();
$payload = $request->json(); // Parsed array for JSON, null otherwise
$method = $request->method();
$ip = $request->ip();

    Body, query, cookies, and files stay separate; input() never falls back to query parameters. Validate every value before use. cookie() reads client cookies, not authenticated session data: use $app->session for that. Headers are case-insensitive, including explicitly constructed test requests. ip() is the direct peer address, matching the existing clientIp() method; forwarded headers are deliberately not trusted. The readonly method/path properties and all existing accessors remain supported.

    isJson() recognizes Content-Type: application/json regardless of case or parameters; it does not inspect Accept, and vendor +json types are not supported. Captured JSON must be an object, with a 1 MiB byte cap and depth limit of 32. Invalid JSON returns 400, oversized bodies return 413, and nested objects become associative arrays. json() returns the already-parsed body, without reading or decoding it again.

    PHP
    use Osoni\Response;

return Response::json(['saved' => true], 201);
return Response::html('<p>' . e($name) . '</p>');
return Response::redirect('/login'); // Local paths only, default 303
return Response::download($authorizedPath, 'report.pdf', 'application/pdf');
return Response::file($authorizedPath, 'application/pdf');

    html() preserves trusted markup; it does not sanitize or escape it. Use escaped template output or e()/Html for untrusted values.

    download() sends an attachment; file() displays inline. Both accept a local regular-file path, reject stream wrappers, and stream without buffering the entire file. The optional MIME override avoids automatic detection; otherwise the native fileinfo extension is required. Download names must be UTF-8, without paths/controls, and at most 255 bytes. Responses use safe ASCII fallback and UTF-8 filename* headers.

    Authorize access and resolve a trusted path first. These generic factories do not implement a storage root or prevent an authorized caller from selecting another local file (including via symlinks). Never use Response::file($request->input('path')). For framework-managed uploads, continue using $app->uploads->download($storedKey, $filename) after checking ownership; it retains its existing storage confinement and response behavior. Generated documents still support their existing in-memory download().

    Missing files/directories return 404; unreadable files and delivery failures throw. Files should remain stable until delivery finishes: no locking, byte-range requests, or conditional caching is introduced. File responses retain no-store, nosniff, and a restrictive sandbox CSP to prevent active content behaving like application HTML. HEAD returns metadata without content; 1xx, 204, and 304 also omit bodies. Sessions are persisted before delivery. Pre-output delivery errors become logged error responses; errors after output starts are logged and rethrown, not replaced with a misleading success body.

    Testing without PHP globals

    Inject query/body/headers/cookies through the existing constructor, then use the normal router or Application::handle():

    PHP
    use Osoni\Request;
use Osoni\Response;
use Osoni\Router;

$request = new Request(
    'POST',
    '/greet',
    query: ['page' => '2'],
    body: ['name' => 'Ada'],
    headers: ['Content-Type' => 'application/json'],
    ip: '127.0.0.1',
    cookies: ['session' => 'test-value'],
);
$router = new Router();
$router->post('/greet', static fn (Request $request): Response =>
    Response::json(['name' => $request->input('name')]));
$response = $router->dispatch($request);

assert($response->status === 200);
assert(json_decode($response->body, true, 32, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR) === ['name' => 'Ada']);

    Construction takes already-parsed body arrays; setting a JSON header does not decode a raw string. It never reads globals or normalizes the path. Direct router tests bypass sessions/CSRF; use the application flow to test those policies. For HTML/JSON, inspect readonly body, status, and headers. Streaming file responses have an empty body and initial file metadata in headers; test delivered bytes through HTTP or isolated output capture. Controllers should return responses, not call send() themselves.

    Data Transformation and Mapping

    Osoni\Data connects structured reading, explicit transformation, validation and export in one lightweight, HTTP-independent pipeline:

    PHP
    use Osoni\Data;

$customers = Data::read('customers.csv')
    ->filter(static fn (array $row): bool => $row['active'] === '1')
    ->map(static fn (array $row): array => [
        'name' => trim($row['name']),
        'email' => trim($row['email']),
    ])
    ->validate([
        '*.name' => 'required|string|max:100',
        '*.email' => 'required|email',
    ])
    ->toArray();

    Bootstrap loads Data; independent scripts can explicitly require framework/Data.php. No Composer, container, automatic class discovery or model property assignment is introduced.

    Explicit shapes and pipeline behavior

    • Data::from($array) wraps an existing array.
    • Data::read($path, $options) reuses all FileReader formats, options, parsing errors and security limits.
    • filter($callback) calls callback($value, $key), requiring a boolean. Lists are reindexed after filtering; associative keys are preserved.
    • map($callback) maps each entry, preserving keys.
    • transform($mapper) maps the whole array, requiring an array result.
    • validate($rules, $messages, $attributes) validates the whole array and retains only fields covered by rules.
    • toArray() returns the current values.
    • write($path, $options) writes the current array and returns the pipeline.
    • insertStatements($table, $driver) builds parameterized insert statements and bindings without executing them.

    This is an eager, copy-on-write array pipeline. Every transformation returns a new pipeline; previous arrays remain unchanged. It is not a streaming collection, and callbacks are trusted application code. Objects and PHP reference-linked values are not deep-cloned: avoid mutating them in callbacks if you need snapshot isolation. Callback exceptions propagate unchanged. For large CSV streaming, keep using FileReader::iterate().

    Validation does not guess whether a document is a list. For one record use name/email; for a top-level record list use *.name/*.email; for nested records use users.*.email. The existing ValidationException exposes concrete failed paths, such as 1.email. Failed rows are never silently dropped. CSV values remain strings until you deliberately convert them. As with the validator, unknown fields are pruned and arrays require explicit descendant rules; validating an empty rule map produces an empty result.

    XML-to-JSON transformation

    The XML reader exposes @attributes, @text and @children, not guessed business records. Supply a mapper to choose the desired shape:

    PHP
    $mapper = static fn (array $document): array => array_map(
    static fn (array $node): array => [
        'id' => $node['@attributes']['id'],
        'name' => $node['@children']['name'][0]['@text'],
    ],
    $document['customers']['@children']['customer'],
);

Data::read('input.xml')
    ->transform($mapper)
    ->validate(['*.id' => 'required|integer', '*.name' => 'required|string'])
    ->write('output.json');

    This example expects a <customers> root with repeated <customer id="..."> elements containing <name>. Validate/check source structure in your mapper when the input schema is not guaranteed. Namespaced nodes retain the existing {URI}local keys; no namespace information is implicitly flattened.

    Rule classes and DTO factories

    Class names are explicit contracts, not constructor reflection:

    PHP
    final class UserRules
{
    public static function rules(): array
    {
        return ['name' => 'required|string', 'email' => 'required|email'];
    }
}

final class UserDto
{
    private function __construct(
        public readonly string $name,
        public readonly string $email,
    ) {}

    public static function fromArray(array $data): self
    {
        return new self($data['name'], $data['email']);
    }
}

// Require these classes explicitly before use.
$payload = $request->json();
if ($payload === null) {
    throw new \Osoni\HttpException(415, 'Use Content-Type: application/json.');
}

$validated = Data::from($payload)->validate(UserRules::class)->toArray();
$user = Data::from([$validated])->map(UserDto::class)->toArray()[0];

    map() always operates on entries: wrap a single record in a list for DTO mapping. Data::from($payload)->map(UserDto::class) would map its field values, not the whole record, and fails when those values are not arrays. A whole-array transform() must still return an array. Rule classes expose public static rules(): array; mapping classes expose public static fromArray(array). Classes must already be loaded; dependencies belong in trusted callbacks or factories, not implicit discovery.

    DTO objects may appear in toArray() but are not automatically serialized, hydrated into models, or accepted by writers. Convert them to deliberate scalar arrays before exporting or validating again:

    PHP
    $export = Data::from([$user])->map(static fn (UserDto $user): array => [
    'name' => $user->name,
    'email' => $user->email,
]);
$export->write('users.json');

    Writers and safety

    Output supports JSON, CSV, XML and YAML/YML, detected by extension:

    PHP
    Data::from($customers)->write('customers.csv', ['delimiter' => ';']);
Data::from($customers)->write('customers.yaml'); // Requires ext-yaml
Data::from(['name' => 'Ada'])->write('customer.xml', ['root' => 'customer']);
Data::from($customers)->write('output.data', ['format' => 'json']);
Data::from([['Ada', 30]])->write('rows.csv', ['headers' => false]);

    Writers reuse Documents/DocumentFile::save(). They do not overwrite existing files or create parent directories. Operational errors propagate; invalid options and unsupported formats fail explicitly. No existing file is replaced on validation/encoding failure.

    CSV expects a list of row arrays with identical column keys in the same order. Headers default true and require nonempty string column names. Positional rows require headers=false. Cells must be scalar/null, not nested arrays. The existing CSV formula protection is on by default and may prefix risky strings with '; use protect_formulas=false only for a deliberately trusted, non-spreadsheet workflow. Delimiters match Documents::csv().

    XML uses the existing generic array-to-element exporter, root document by default. It is not a lossless writer for the XML reader's attributes, namespaces or mixed-content representation: transform those nodes into your chosen output shape first. JSON follows PHP array shape: lists encode as arrays, associative arrays as objects; an empty PHP array encodes as []. No original empty-object identity is retained.

    YAML/YML output requires the native YAML extension, as reading does. Only plain scalar/array data is emitted; no PHP object tags or custom serialization are introduced. All formats reject DTOs/resources, invalid text, non-finite numbers, cycles, depth above 64 and graphs above 100000 values. Text uses the existing UTF-8/XML-safe document rules, even for JSON/YAML.

    max_bytes bounds published output, default 16 MiB, configurable from 1 byte to 256 MiB. Encoding occurs in memory before the byte check; it is not a peak memory guarantee. Input bounds remain the reader's own limits. Storage is separate: Data::read/write accept local paths, not remote storage keys; use explicit private temporary files or the existing storage byte API when needed.

    File Storage Abstraction

    Use the application-owned $app->storage service so handlers do not depend on the physical location of their files:

    PHP
    $app->storage->put('documents/test.pdf', $content);
$content = $app->storage->get('documents/test.pdf');
$exists = $app->storage->exists('documents/test.pdf');
$deleted = $app->storage->delete('documents/test.pdf');

    put() returns void and overwrites an existing key. get() returns exact binary bytes, including valid empty content; a missing file throws RuntimeException. exists() returns a boolean. delete() returns true for acknowledged deletion, false for absence. Invalid keys/configuration throw InvalidArgumentException; permissions, authentication, transport, provider errors and unsafe filesystem paths fail explicitly. A cloud HTTP 404 is treated as missing, so keep the selected bucket/container provisioned.

    The service is not static, matching the framework's application-owned services and avoiding mutable global configuration. Independent usage works without bootstrap/Composer:

    PHP
    require_once __DIR__ . '/framework/Storage.php';

$storage = new \Osoni\Storage(__DIR__, [
    'driver' => 'local',
    'max_bytes' => 16777216,
]);
$storage->put('documents/readme.txt', 'Hello');

    Common configuration and keys

    DOTENV
    STORAGE_DRIVER=local
STORAGE_MAX_BYTES=16777216
STORAGE_TIMEOUT=30
STORAGE_CA_FILE=

    Configuration lives in config/storage.php; .env.example lists every setting. Existing installations can add only the settings they need; the real .env is never overwritten. Construction validates configuration without creating directories or connecting remotely. Choose local, sftp, s3, or azure; changing the driver does not migrate existing data.

    Keys are relative UTF-8 paths, at most 1024 bytes, with segments at most 255 bytes. Use forward slashes; do not use leading/trailing slashes, empty/dot segments, hidden filenames, backslashes, percent escapes, #, controls, Windows-reserved characters/device names, or trailing dots/spaces. This shared portable subset behaves consistently across all drivers. Keys are validated, not silently normalized. Case sensitivity still follows the underlying filesystem/provider; avoid names that differ only by case.

    max_bytes applies to put() and get(), from 1 byte through 256 MiB, default 16 MiB. Reads are bounded; arbitrary binary/empty files are supported. The API uses strings, not streaming handles, so allow memory for the content and transport buffers. Large/multipart transfers are intentionally not supplied. STORAGE_TIMEOUT is the S3/Azure HTTPS deadline, 1..300 seconds; SFTP has native SSH2 transport behavior rather than a guaranteed per-operation deadline.

    Local driver

    Files live in **STORAGE_PATH/files**, separate from uploads, logs and compiled views. storage:prepare prepares this directory when local is selected:

    Terminal
    php osoni storage:prepare

    Local directories are created lazily on writes, with POSIX 0700 directories and 0600 files. Windows uses inherited NTFS ACLs: restrict them to the service identity. Reads/exists/deletes do not create missing directories. The driver rejects symlink ancestors/entries and storage within (or containing) public/. Writes use a same-directory temporary file and rename; failed writes do not publish partial content.

    Use a trusted, exclusively managed root. Path checks cannot prevent hostile concurrent OS users from replacing directories between validation and use. No hard-link isolation or cross-writer transaction/locking guarantee is added. Files remain private; authorize access before exposing their contents.

    SFTP driver

    Requires the native ext-ssh2 extension and an existing remote directory:

    DOTENV
    STORAGE_DRIVER=sftp
STORAGE_SFTP_HOST=sftp.example.test
STORAGE_SFTP_PORT=22
STORAGE_SFTP_USERNAME=application
STORAGE_SFTP_PASSWORD=
STORAGE_SFTP_ROOT=/data/application
STORAGE_SFTP_FINGERPRINT=
