STORAGE_SFTP_PUBLIC_KEY=/private/keys/application.pub
STORAGE_SFTP_PRIVATE_KEY=/private/keys/application
STORAGE_SFTP_PASSPHRASE=

    Set the fingerprint to an independently verified 40-character hexadecimal SHA-1 host-key fingerprint, without colons, before connecting. The pin format comes from ext-ssh2; do not learn/trust it automatically on first connection. The host is verified before credentials are sent. Prefer RSA PEM key-file authentication:

    Terminal
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 3072 -m PEM -f application

    Key files must be local/readable and the RSA PEM private file at most 64 KiB. OpenSSH-format/ECDSA user keys are not accepted: native SSH2 compatibility is not reliable across supported runtimes. To use password authentication, configure STORAGE_SFTP_PASSWORD and leave both key-file settings empty. Never put actual passwords/private keys in the repository.

    The driver creates child directories, refuses symlinks via remote lstat, and checks directory listings so permission/network errors do not become false missing-file results. Use least-privilege server permissions/chroot; the remote root and its ancestors must be real directories. Operations use native SSH2 blocking behavior: supervise processes with an external deadline when needed.

    Writes stage a 0600 temporary file. Replacing an existing file stages the old file as a backup, publishes the new one, then removes the backup; a failed publish attempts restoration. Unlike local rename-overwrite, this is not atomic for concurrent readers/writers. A process crash can leave temporary/ backup files or a gap; use an application-specific recovery policy and do not run competing writers for the same key.

    S3-compatible driver

    Requires native ext-curl, an existing bucket and path-style addressing:

    DOTENV
    STORAGE_DRIVER=s3
STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT=https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
STORAGE_S3_BUCKET=application-files
STORAGE_S3_REGION=us-east-1
STORAGE_S3_ACCESS_KEY=
STORAGE_S3_SECRET_KEY=
STORAGE_S3_SESSION_TOKEN=

    Use the provider's trusted HTTPS origin and exact signing region. Requests use AWS Signature V4 with payload SHA-256, including optional temporary credential tokens. Private S3-compatible endpoints are supported, but HTTP, credential-bearing URLs, endpoint paths/query/fragment and redirects are not. For private certificate authorities set a readable STORAGE_CA_FILE; TLS certificate/hostname verification cannot be disabled.

    Provision least-privilege object read/write/delete permissions. exists() uses HEAD; delete() probes HEAD first, so deletion also requires read access. A successful delete is not proof that another writer did not race it. Versioned buckets may retain previous versions/delete markers according to their policies. Multipart uploads, public ACLs, credential discovery/automatic refresh, presigned URLs and bucket creation are not implemented.

    Azure Blob driver

    Requires native ext-curl, an existing container and Shared Key access:

    DOTENV
    STORAGE_DRIVER=azure
STORAGE_AZURE_ACCOUNT=applicationaccount
STORAGE_AZURE_CONTAINER=documents
STORAGE_AZURE_KEY=
STORAGE_AZURE_ENDPOINT=

    The key is the base64 account key (64 decoded bytes), not a connection string or SAS token. The default endpoint is https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net; an optional trusted HTTPS origin supports sovereign/custom hosts. Native HMAC-SHA256 Shared Key signs BlockBlob requests using REST version 2023-11-03. Delete includes blob snapshots; versions, soft deletion and retention still follow Azure policy.

    Shared Key can grant broad account access: isolate accounts and protect/ rotate credentials externally. Microsoft recommends Entra managed identities where possible, but Entra/SAS/managed-identity credential acquisition is not implemented here. No container provisioning, public access changes or chunked block uploads are performed.

    File readers, responses and testing

    FileReader::read()/iterate() operate on local paths, not storage keys. Stored JSON can be decoded directly from bytes:

    PHP
    $data = json_decode($app->storage->get('imports/users.json'), true, 64, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

    For CSV/XML/YAML, explicitly materialize retrieved content into a trusted private temporary file with the correct extension, invoke FileReader, and remove the temporary file in finally. Storage does not bypass the readers' parsing limits or extension requirements. CSV streaming remains local-file streaming; remote get() buffers bounded content.

    Logs, sessions, compiled views, migrations, uploads and generated documents keep their existing APIs/locations. Remote storage does not make a local Response::file()/download() path available. Small remote files can be returned through a deliberately authorized binary response; do not expose storage endpoints, credentials or raw user-selected keys.

    Tests use isolated local roots, verified loopback HTTPS fixtures, signing checks, missing/error cases, binary data, bounds and symlink rejection. The optional real SFTP integration uses a private loopback OpenSSH process, throwaway keys and ext-ssh2:

    Terminal
    OSONI_TEST_SSHD_BINARY=/usr/sbin/sshd php osoni test

    It runs in the Linux CI SFTP job; standard tests remain Windows/Linux compatible without requiring SSH2. Cloud tests do not contact real AWS/Azure accounts. Verify your provider's endpoint, permissions and retention policies before deploying. To add a format-independent backend, implement Osoni\Storage\DriverInterface, explicitly load/register it in Storage, and run the shared contract tests; no implicit driver discovery is used.

    Application Logging

    Central exception handling

    Osoni\ExceptionHandler is shared by the web lifecycle and API dispatch:

    PHP
    $response = $app->exceptions->render($exception, $request);
// Return the response; Application::run() normally does this automatically.

    It handles Throwable, including native PHP errors, without Composer or a process-global exception handler. Request-capture, route, session-persistence, and pre-output file-delivery failures use the same mapping. Startup failures also use it once loaded; earlier bootstrap failures use a minimal safe JSON fallback. Failures after output starts are logged without appending another error body. Health/readiness status responses and CLI errors keep their existing specialized behavior.

    Development diagnostics require both settings:

    DOTENV
    APP_ENV=local
APP_DEBUG=true

    Server failures then return HTTP 500 (or the explicit server-error status) with text/plain; charset=UTF-8, containing exception class, message, file, line, stack trace, and a limited request summary (method, path, direct IP). Trace arguments, body/query values, headers, cookies and uploaded-file data are omitted. Failures before capture say request context is unavailable. Exception messages and route paths can still contain sensitive information: never expose local debug mode to untrusted users.

    Production and all non-local environments suppress diagnostic details, even if APP_DEBUG=true is mistakenly configured. With local debug disabled, the same privacy behavior applies. Browser requests get an HTML error page. JSON/API requests retain error.code (INTERNAL_ERROR), the generic message An unexpected error occurred., and error.status. No exception class, private message, file, line, stack trace, request payload or previous exception is returned. Every server-error status, including an explicitly thrown HttpException(503, ...), uses the generic message; Retry-After can be retained, while arbitrary server-error headers are discarded. Server failures are reported once through the existing logger; its safe report omits exception messages, traces, arguments and request data.

    Expected 4xx failures use HTML pages for browser requests, validation returns 422, missing records return generic 404, and Allow/Retry-After survive. API/JSON errors include code: "HTTP_422" (or the relevant status), status, message, and existing validation details. Only put deliberately public text in HTTP exceptions and custom validation messages; they are not automatically sanitized for secrets.

    Custom error pages

    To customize a status, add app/views/errors/http-404.osoni.php (or http-404.php). Use the same naming pattern for 500, 403, or any other 4xx/5xx status. The template receives $status, $title, and $message; for 5xx errors the message is always generic. For example:

    HTML
    <!doctype html>
<html lang="en-US">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>{{ $status }} {{ $title }}</title></head>
<body>
    <main>
        <h1>{{ $title }}</h1>
        <p>{{ $message }}</p>
        <p><a href="/">Go to the home page</a></p>
    </main>
</body>
</html>

    In plain PHP templates, escape text with e(). Keep error templates independent of session and database services so they can render when those services fail. If the view is missing or throws, Osoni uses its built-in HTML page and keeps the original status and protocol headers. An exception from the view is logged. These pages apply to exceptions handled by the application, not responses returned explicitly by routes, server-generated errors, or startup failures before the application runs. /api requests, requests with Content-Type: application/json, and local debug diagnostics bypass HTML views.

    For independent usage:

    PHP
    use Osoni\ExceptionHandler;

$handler = new ExceptionHandler('production', false, $logger);
$response = $handler->render($exception); // Request context is optional.

    Application::errorResponse() and Api::errorResponse() remain compatibility adapters. Prefer $app->exceptions for environment-aware handling; the static web adapter's explicit debug=true opts into local diagnostics without reading environment configuration. Without a View, the standalone handler and static web adapter retain plain text for 4xx and generic JSON for 5xx. Local API server failures also become diagnostic plain text when debug is explicitly enabled.

    Use the native $app->log service for structured application logs. No Composer, PSR interface, database migration, or external logging package is required.

    PHP
    $app->log->info('Report created.', ['report_id' => 42]);
$app->log->warning('Delivery delayed.', ['attempt' => 2]);
$app->log->error('Processing failed.', ['exception' => $exception]);
$app->log->log('notice', 'Import completed.', ['rows' => 120]);

    Available methods/levels, from lowest to highest severity, are debug, info, notice, warning, error, critical, alert, and emergency. Configure the minimum level and retention in .env:

    DOTENV
    LOG_LEVEL=debug
LOG_RETENTION_DAYS=5

    The corresponding application configuration keys are log_level and log_retention_days. Retention must be an integer from 1 through 3650. Levels are lowercase and validated when the application is constructed. Standalone usage is also supported:

    PHP
    $logger = new \Osoni\Logger($app->root, retentionDays: 5, minimumLevel: 'info');
$logger->notice('Maintenance completed.');

    Logs are newline-delimited JSON in storage/logs/app-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl. Each entry contains a UTC ISO-style timestamp with microseconds, level, message, and context. Embedded line breaks are JSON-escaped; a message cannot inject a second log record. Directories are created lazily with 0700 and files/locks use 0600 on Linux. On Windows, restrict inherited NTFS ACLs to the administrator and PHP service user. Storage stays outside public/, rejects symlinked directories/files, and is ignored by the existing Git rules. Never expose the storage directory through a web-server alias.

    Concurrent writers serialize through a private file lock. After each written entry, retention removes only matching daily log files older than the retained UTC calendar window: five days means today plus the previous four dates. Unrelated files and symlinks are not removed. Cleanup runs on writes, not on a background schedule; filtered entries do not trigger cleanup. Files are daily, not size-rotated: provision disk space, choose an appropriate minimum level, and monitor write failures.

    Context supports nested arrays, scalars, null, and exceptions. Sensitive keys containing password, secret, token, authorization, cookie, credential, or API/ private-key names are recursively replaced with [REDACTED]. Exceptions are reduced to class, source file, and line; exception messages, traces, previous exceptions, and arguments are deliberately omitted because they may contain credentials or request data. Context is limited to eight nested levels and each serialized entry to 64 KiB. Unsupported objects/resources, invalid UTF-8, nonfinite numbers, recursive/deep context, or oversized entries throw explicitly. Messages are plain text; there is no placeholder interpolation.

    Redaction is not a general secret detector. It does not inspect arbitrary message text or values under unrelated keys. Do not log passwords, tokens, connection strings, full request objects, uploaded contents, or personal data. Choose safe, minimal context fields explicitly.

    Unexpected web/API errors are logged automatically through the configured application logger while existing public error responses remain unchanged. Server-side HTTP exceptions (5xx) are also logged; ordinary validation, authentication, and other 4xx responses are not. API errors caught inside the API router use the same logger. CLI command failures after application startup are logged except invalid-argument/usage errors. There is no automatic access log or request-body/header/query logging.

    Direct logger writes throw on failure. Automatic exception reporting catches logging failures and explicitly reports a safe diagnostic to PHP's server log without recursively invoking the file logger. Errors before application initialization also use the PHP server log; the CLI still prints its error and exits with a failure status. This service does not install global error/exception handlers or capture engine fatal errors/shutdown events: keep PHP's log_errors and server monitoring configured. A minimum level above error also filters automatic application-error entries.

    File Uploads

    Web routes accept native PHP multipart/form-data uploads through Request. Use an explicit list of allowed filename extensions for each upload handler. There is deliberately no allow-all default. The default per-file size limit is 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes).

    Configure the application default in .env:

    DOTENV
    UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES=2097152

    This must be a positive integer number of bytes. It configures $app->uploads->maxBytes through upload_max_bytes in the application config. It does not change PHP's upload_max_filesize or post_max_size.

    Supported types are jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, pdf, txt, csv, docx, and xlsx. Use lowercase extensions without a dot. Uploaded extension matching is case-insensitive. PHP/script files, HTML, SVG, arbitrary ZIP archives, and legacy .doc/.xls files are not supported.

    Receiving and Storing a File

    Register a protected web route in routes/web.php:

    PHP
    use Osoni\HttpException;
use Osoni\Request;
use Osoni\Response;

$router->post('/documents', $app->auth->protect(
    static function (Request $request) use ($app): Response {
        $file = $request->file('document');
        if ($file === null) {
            throw new HttpException(422, 'Choose a document to upload.');
        }
        $stored = $app->uploads->store(
            $file,
            allowedTypes: ['pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx'],
        );

        // Persist these values with the current user's ID in your own model.
        // Delete the stored upload if your database write subsequently fails.
        return Response::json([
            'key' => $stored->key,
            'name' => $stored->originalName,
            'mime' => $stored->mimeType,
            'size' => $stored->size,
        ], 201);
    },
));

    In a Osoni template, submit a multipart form with the normal CSRF field. Pass 'session' => $app->session in the view's render data:

    HTML
    <form action="/documents" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
    @csrf($session)
    <label for="document">Document</label>
    <input id="document" name="document" type="file" accept=".pdf,.docx,.xlsx" required>
    <button type="submit">Upload document</button>
</form>

    The browser's accept attribute is only a selection hint, not validation. JavaScript clients may send the CSRF token in X-CSRF-Token; let the browser set the multipart boundary when using FormData.

    file() returns an UploadedFile or null for a missing field/no file selection. If more than one file is supplied to a single-file accessor, it throws HTTP 400. files() always returns a list; missing selections are omitted. One-dimensional documents[] and keyed file lists are supported; deeper nested upload fields are rejected with HTTP 400. Nonempty PHP upload failures remain accessible and are reported by validation.

    The uploaded object exposes originalName, clientMediaType, and PHP's error code. Client path components are removed from the original name; the remaining UTF-8 name must contain 1 to 255 bytes without control characters. Treat this name as display metadata and escape it in HTML. The client media type is explicitly untrusted and is never used to approve or serve a file.

    store() validates before writing. It returns a StoredUpload with read-only key, originalName, mimeType, and actual byte size properties. It uses is_uploaded_file() and move_uploaded_file(): arbitrary local server files and CLI-created temporary files cannot be passed off as uploads. Each file receives a cryptographically random 64-hex-character key plus its validated extension. Files are stored as storage/uploads/<random-id>/file.<extension>, never under the client's name, so equal original names cannot overwrite one another.

    Storage directories are created on demand with 0700 permissions and files receive 0600 on Linux. On Windows, restrict inherited NTFS ACLs to the administrator and PHP service user. The storage location is outside public/; symlinked storage directories and symlinked stored files are rejected. Upload contents are ignored by the existing storage/ Git ignore rule.

    There is no automatic attachment database table or ownership model. Persist the storage key, display name, size, media type, and owner as your application requires. Keys locate files; they are not authorization credentials. No public upload/download routes are installed by this feature.

    Multiple Files and Custom Limits

    PHP
    $files = $request->files('documents');
if ($files === [] || count($files) > 5) {
    throw new \Osoni\HttpException(422, 'Choose between one and five files.');
}

// Check every file before starting a batch write.
foreach ($files as $file) {
    $metadata = $app->uploads->validate($file, ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png'], maxBytes: 524288);
}
foreach ($files as $file) {
    $stored = $app->uploads->store($file, ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png'], maxBytes: 524288);
    // Persist each file and its owner.
}

    Use an input with name="documents[]" and the multiple attribute. $app->uploads->validate($file, $allowedTypes) performs the same checks as store() without moving the file, using the configured default, returning extension, canonical mime, and actual byte size. The optional positive integer maxBytes overrides the configured per-file default; it does not raise PHP or web-server limits. Empty files are rejected. Calling $file->validate() directly is standalone validation and retains a 2 MiB default unless you explicitly pass maxBytes; use the application service for environment-aware validation.

    Batches are not filesystem/database transactions. Prevalidating a batch avoids starting writes for an already-invalid file, but disk or database failures can still occur later. Track successful keys and clean them up if the operation must be all-or-nothing. Enforce application-specific file-count, combined-byte, user-quota, and rate limits.

    Protected Downloads and Deletion

    After authenticating a user and loading an attachment record belonging to that user, return:

    PHP
    return $app->uploads->download($attachment['storage_key'], $attachment['original_name']);

    Register the download action with $app->auth->protect(...) and perform the ownership/record authorization check before calling download(). Never authorize access just because someone knows a random storage key. download() itself is a storage operation, not an authorization service. Its optional filename defaults to download.<extension>; the original name must come from your persisted metadata if you want to restore it.

    Downloads reuse the normal attachment response: canonical media type, UTF-8-safe filename headers, correct byte length, nosniff, and no-store. HEAD requests omit the response body. Invalid keys, missing files, and symlinked file targets produce HTTP 404. Files are read into memory to build the response; bound upload limits accordingly.

    After the same authentication and ownership checks, a CSRF-protected POST or DELETE handler may call:

    PHP
    $app->uploads->delete($attachment['storage_key']);

    This removes only that stored file and its random directory. Coordinate deletion of your database metadata explicitly; deleting an attachment record does not automatically delete the file, and deleting a file does not update your database.

    Validation and Deployment Limits

    • Validation checks the real temporary file size, allowed extension, and server-detected media type using native fileinfo, not client-provided size/type claims.
    • Images also undergo a native header/dimension check. This is not a full image decode, re-encoding service, or pixel-count limit; add application image-dimension limits before further processing untrusted images.
    • DOCX/XLSX files must be ZIP packages containing the matching main document, content-type, and relationship entries. Checks reject macro-named entries, encrypted entries, unsafe archive paths, more than 1,000 entries, entries larger than 10 MiB, or a combined declared expansion larger than 20 MiB. Archives are not extracted. These are bounded package-shape checks, not complete Office schema validation or a guarantee of harmless content.
    • MIME/header checks are not malware scanning or content sanitization. PDFs and Office documents may contain active content or external links. Uploaded CSV files may contain spreadsheet formulas; validation does not rewrite their contents. Add quarantine/scanning if your deployment requires it. Do not execute, include, extract, or render uploaded content inline simply because it passed validation.
    • file_uploads must be enabled. Configure a writable PHP upload_tmp_dir and writable private storage. Enable native fileinfo; Office checks additionally need zip.
    • PHP's upload_max_filesize must accommodate the per-file limit; post_max_size must accommodate all files, form fields, and multipart overhead. For a single 2 MiB file, a typical starting point is upload_max_filesize=2M and post_max_size=8M. Configure these in the PHP configuration used by your actual web server.
    • PHP's max_file_uploads, max_input_vars, and max_input_nesting_level can limit parsed fields. PHP may omit files/fields beyond its parsing limits; handlers must check required fields and expected file counts.
    • Web-server/reverse-proxy body-size limits also apply. Raising framework maxBytes cannot bypass them.

    The request layer returns HTTP 413 when a POST exceeds PHP's configured post_max_size, rather than treating PHP's discarded body as an empty form. Per-file PHP size failures and framework size failures also return 413; partial files, disallowed types, invalid images/packages, empty files, and untrusted local-file sources return 422. Malformed file-field structures return

    1. Server receive/storage failures throw and use the standard logged,

    generic HTTP 500 response. Application-required file errors should be explicitly reported by the handler, as in the example above.

    Multipart support is for normal POST web routes, preserving session/CSRF behavior. The separate /api/* router remains JSON-only and rejects multipart bodies with HTTP 415 (or 413 when its request-size limit is exceeded). Native PHP does not populate this API for raw PUT/PATCH uploads, chunked upload protocols, remote URLs, or base64 JSON file payloads.

    String Manipulation

    Use the native $app->strings service, or instantiate Osoni\Strings after bootstrap. It accepts UTF-8 strings and throws InvalidArgumentException for malformed encoding instead of silently replacing bytes. No Composer dependencies are used. Case conversion requires mbstring; grapheme operations, naming helpers, and slug transliteration require intl. The service is stateless and construction does not require either extension.

    PHP
    $strings = $app->strings;
echo $strings->upper('Straße');                   // STRASSE
echo $strings->lower('ÉLÈVE');                    // élève
echo $strings->title('hello WORLD');              // Hello World
echo $strings->trim("\u{00a0} Ada \u{2003}");      // Ada
echo $strings->length("e\u{0301}");               // 1 visible character
echo $strings->slice('Hello world', 6);           // world
echo $strings->slice('Hello world', -5);          // world

    length(), slice(), and truncate() use Unicode grapheme clusters: combining accents and joined emoji are not split into individual code points. Offsets are zero-based; negative offsets count from the end. A null slice length includes the remainder; a negative length omits that many characters from the end. Out-of-range offsets return an empty string. Case conversion follows Unicode mappings, not locale-specific Turkish/Dutch rules, and can expand characters (ß becomes SS). No method changes global locale, encoding, or input data.

    Matching, Extraction, and Replacement

    PHP
    $strings->contains('Hello café', 'café');         // true
$strings->startsWith('report.csv', 'report');     // true
$strings->endsWith('report.csv', '.csv');          // true
$strings->before('one/two/three', '/');            // one
$strings->after('one/two/three', '/');             // two/three
$strings->replace('Hello Ada, Ada!', 'Ada', 'Lin'); // Hello Lin, Lin!

    Matching is literal and case-sensitive, without regex interpretation or automatic Unicode normalization. Visually identical composed/decomposed characters may therefore differ. Empty needles match in contains(), startsWith(), and endsWith(), including against an empty string. before() and after() use the first occurrence and return the original text when absent. Empty extraction delimiters and replacement searches throw; an empty replacement deletes each occurrence. replace() changes all nonoverlapping occurrences. Unicode whitespace trimming removes leading and trailing whitespace/separators, not internal whitespace or zero-width marks.

    Truncation, Slugs, and Naming

    PHP
    $strings->truncate('Hello world', 8);             // Hello...
$strings->truncate('Hello world', 5, '');         // Hello
$strings->truncate('Hello world', 2);             // ..
$strings->slug(' Crème brûlée! ');                // creme-brulee
$strings->slug('Hello World', '_');               // hello_world
$strings->snake('HTTPServerID');                  // http_server_id
$strings->camel('HTTP_server_ID');                // httpServerId
$strings->studly('hello-world');                  // HelloWorld

    The truncation limit includes the suffix (default ...), measured in visible characters. A zero limit produces empty text when truncation is needed; negative limits throw. An oversized suffix is itself cut to fit. Short text is returned unchanged, with no added suffix.

    Slugs transliterate through ICU into lowercase ASCII letters/digits, collapse other characters into a hyphen or underscore, and trim outer separators. Punctuation-only or untransliterable input can yield an empty slug. ICU versions can change transliteration results. Slugs are not guaranteed unique: validate the result and enforce application/database uniqueness. They are not file-path validation or authorization.

    Naming helpers split separator runs, lowercase-to-uppercase boundaries, and acronym-to-word boundaries (HTTPServer becomes HTTP, Server). They retain Unicode letters/marks/numbers, normalize word casing, and do not transliterate. Separator-only input becomes empty. Digits remain with their preceding word unless followed by an uppercase letter.

    Cryptographic Random Strings

    PHP
    $token = $strings->random();                      // 32 alphanumeric characters
$hex = $strings->random(64, '0123456789abcdef');   // 64 hex characters

    random() uses native random_bytes() and rejection sampling to avoid alphabet-selection bias, not rand() or mt_rand(). Length must be 1..65536; the alphabet must contain 2..94 distinct printable non-space ASCII characters. Duplicate characters, Unicode alphabets, whitespace, and invalid lengths throw. Random-source failures propagate. Choose sufficient length/alphabet entropy for your use case; this does not add expiry, hashing, uniqueness guarantees, or authorization. Continue using the built-in authentication/API token services for those flows, and do not log secrets.

    Using Strings in Views

    $strings is reserved and available automatically in both PHP and Osoni views, including layouts and partials. Render data cannot override it.

    HTML
    <h1>{{ $strings->title($title) }}</h1>
<p>{{ $strings->truncate($description, 160) }}</p>

    Plain PHP views should use e($strings->upper($title)). String operations do not escape HTML, sanitize rich text, or make SQL/URLs safe; keep normal context-appropriate output escaping and parameter binding.

    Date/Time Utility

    Use the static Osoni\Date utility for practical native date operations:

    PHP
    use Osoni\Date;

$now = Date::now();
$date = Date::parse('2026-11-14 12:30:00');
$later = Date::addDays(5, $date);
$start = Date::startOfDay($date);
$text = Date::format('Y-m-d', $date);
$relative = Date::diffForHumans('2026-11-13T12:00:00Z', '2026-11-14T12:00:00Z');
// "1 day ago"

// Omitting a base date uses current time:
Date::addDays(5);
Date::startOfDay();
Date::format('Y-m-d');
Date::diffForHumans(); // "just now"

    Bootstrap loads the utility; standalone scripts can explicitly require framework/Date.php. No Composer or Intl extension is needed. Date-producing methods return native DateTimeImmutable objects, so arithmetic never changes your original date. This is a static utility, not a stateful fluent wrapper.

    Parsing and timezone rules

    parse() accepts native DateTimeInterface, integer Unix timestamps in seconds (including zero/negative values), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO/SQL date-time strings using T/space, minutes or seconds, optional fractional seconds up to six digits, and an optional Z or +HH:MM/-HH:MM offset.

    Empty strings, numeric timestamp strings, ambiguous locale dates, relative expressions such as tomorrow, invalid calendar dates, and rollover times fail with InvalidArgumentException; they never silently become now. Convert numeric timestamp strings explicitly after validating them.

    Defaults are UTC, not the machine's timezone. Input date objects keep their timezone; offset-bearing strings keep their stated offset. Supply an explicit IANA timezone to interpret timezone-less strings or convert an instant:

    PHP
    $local = Date::parse('2026-11-14 12:30:00', 'Europe/Amsterdam');
$utc = Date::parse($local, 'UTC');
$today = Date::startOfDay($local);
$display = Date::format('Y-m-d H:i:s P', $local);
$configured = Date::now($app->config['timezone'] ?? 'UTC');

    No helper changes PHP's global timezone or reads environment configuration implicitly. Timezone names must be UTC or recognized IANA identifiers, not ambiguous abbreviations/numeric offsets. Explicit offset strings are supported as date input.

    Timezone-less input that lands in a DST gap is rejected. Repeated local times follow PHP's native timezone interpretation; supply an explicit offset when the precise repeated instant matters. addDays() uses calendar days, preserving local wall-time/microseconds where timezone rules allow, not fixed 24-hour durations. A DST day can be 23 or 25 hours; arithmetic landing in a gap follows native normalization. Allowed day offsets are -365000..365000. startOfDay() resets microseconds too; a nonexistent local midnight follows native normalization to a valid time.

    Formatting and human differences

    format() uses PHP date patterns, not ICU: Date::format('Y-m-d H:i', $date). Patterns must be nonempty UTF-8, at most 256 bytes, without control characters. Format results are not HTML-escaped. Use the existing $app->format service for locale-aware date/time output.

    diffForHumans($date, $relativeTo = null) reports past/future direction and the largest whole elapsed-time unit: "2 minutes ago", "in 1 hour", or "just now" for differences below a second. Days are 86400 seconds, months are approximated as 30 days, and years as 365 days; it is not a calendar-month or financial-age calculation. Fractions are truncated, not rounded. The output is concise US English; it is not translated by the application translation service. Providing an explicit reference date makes examples/tests deterministic.

    Application Text Translations

    Use $app->translator for application-owned text. Create an app/lang directory and add one UTF-8 JSON object per locale, using the exact locale spelling in the filename. Keys are flat strings, including dots if desired. For example, create app/lang/en-US.json:

    JSON
    {"welcome": "Hello, {name}!", "nav.home": "Home"}

    Create app/lang/nl-NL.json:

    JSON
    {"welcome": "Hallo, {name}!"}

    In a controller, choose a locale from an application-maintained allowlist before passing it to the service:

    PHP
    $message = $app->translator->get('welcome', ['name' => 'Ada'], 'nl-NL');
// Hallo, Ada!

    When omitted, the locale is APP_LOCALE (default en-US), also used by the formatter. A missing catalog or key falls back to en-US; a missing key there throws. Invalid catalogs and invalid locale tags throw rather than falling back. A standalone new \Osoni\Translator($directory, 'nl-NL', 'en-US') can use a different fallback. Tags have the same syntactic form as formatting locales; filenames are case-sensitive on some systems. Catalogs must be trusted application files, not user uploads.

    The same service is reserved as $translator in PHP and Osoni views, including layouts and includes. For example, in a Osoni view:

    PHP
    {{ $translator->get('welcome', ['name' => $name], $locale) }}

    Osoni escapes the result; use e() in plain PHP views. Replacements use literal {name} placeholders and are not themselves escaped. Translation does not select or persist a visitor's language, change the formatter's locale, translate existing framework messages, or implement plural rules. Pass the chosen locale explicitly to both translation and formatting calls; set the page's HTML lang attribute to match. Supply localized validator messages explicitly as described in the validation section.

    Date, Time, Money, and Decimal Formatting

    The shared $app->format service uses native PHP Intl/ICU without Composer or external packages. Defaults are en-US and UTC; configure them in your local .env:

    DOTENV
    APP_LOCALE=en-US
APP_TIMEZONE=UTC

    The application configuration uses locale and timezone keys. You can also create a standalone formatter:

    PHP
    $format = new \Osoni\Formatter(locale: 'de-DE', timezone: 'Europe/Berlin');

    Use language tags such as en-US, nl-NL, de-DE, fr-FR, hi-IN, or ar-EG. Optional script and region subtags are supported; ICU extensions and locale keywords are not. ICU may fall back to a supported parent locale; an unsupported language throws instead of silently using the machine's default. Use IANA time zone identifiers such as UTC, America/New_York, or Europe/Amsterdam, not ambiguous abbreviations or numeric UTC offsets. Neither formatter creation nor individual calls change PHP's global time zone or Intl's global locale. Missing Intl is reported when formatting is requested, so unrelated framework features do not require it.

    Dates and Times

    PHP
    $date = new \DateTimeImmutable('2026-11-13T15:45:06+00:00');

$app->format->date($date, 'short'); // 11/13/26
$app->format->date($date);          // Nov 13, 2026
$app->format->date($date, 'long');   // November 13, 2026
$app->format->date($date, 'full');   // Friday, November 13, 2026
$app->format->time($date, 'short');
$app->format->dateTime($date);

$app->format->date($date, 'short', locale: 'de-DE'); // 13.11.26
$app->format->dateTime(
    $date,
    locale: 'en-US',
    timezone: 'America/New_York',
    pattern: 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss XXX',
); // 2026-11-13 10:45:06 -05:00

$app->format->dateTime(0, pattern: 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss'); // 1970-01-01 00:00:00

    Inputs are DateTimeInterface objects or integer Unix timestamps in seconds. Strings are intentionally not parsed; construct and validate your dates explicitly. Dates are formatted in the configured or overridden time zone, not necessarily the input object's zone, without mutating that object. IANA daylight-saving rules apply.

    date() and time() default to medium. dateTime() defaults to a medium date and short time. Styles are short, medium, long, and full; for dateTime(), either part may be none. At least one part must be visible unless a custom pattern is supplied.

    The optional pattern uses **ICU syntax, not PHP date() syntax**. For example, yyyy-MM-dd is a numeric date and HH:mm:ss is 24-hour time. Quote literal text using ICU apostrophe rules. A pattern overrides the style layout and must contain 1 to 256 UTF-8 bytes without control characters. Localized punctuation, spacing, and names can vary with the installed ICU version. The calendar is explicitly Gregorian.

    Decimal Numbers and Percentages

    PHP
    $app->format->decimal('1234.5');                       // 1,234.50
$app->format->decimal('1234.5', precision: 3);         // 1,234.500
$app->format->decimal(1234, precision: 0);             // 1,234
$app->format->decimal('1234.5', locale: 'de-DE');       // 1.234,50
$app->format->decimal('12345678.5', locale: 'hi-IN');   // 1,23,45,678.50
$app->format->decimal('1234.5', grouping: false);      // 1234.50
$app->format->decimal('1.005');                        // 1.01
$app->format->decimal('-1.005');                       // -1.01

$app->format->percent('0.125');                       // 12.50%
$app->format->percent('0.125', precision: 1);          // 12.5%
$app->format->percent('0.125', locale: 'de-DE');        // 12,50 %

    Decimal and percent inputs are integers or decimal strings. The precision range is 0 through 20, defaulting to exactly 2 fractional digits. Rounding is half away from zero, performed on strings without binary floating-point conversion. Negative values that round to zero display as positive zero. Percent inputs are ratios: 1 means 100%, not 1%.

    Grouping sizes, decimal/group separators, digits, signs, and percent placement follow ICU locale rules. Some locales use nonbreaking spaces or non-Latin digits, and some do not group four-digit numbers. Do not compare rendered values after replacing those characters with ordinary spaces.

    Money

    PHP
    $app->format->money('1234.565', 'USD');                 // $1,234.57
$app->format->money('1.005', 'USD');                    // $1.01
$app->format->money('1234.5', 'EUR', locale: 'de-DE');   // 1.234,50 €
$app->format->money('1234.5', 'JPY');                   // ¥1,235
$app->format->money('1.2345', 'KWD');                   // KWD 1.235
$app->format->money('1234.5', grouping: false);         // $1234.50

$app->format->moneyMinor(12345, 'USD');                 // $123.45
$app->format->moneyMinor(-1, 'USD');                    // -$0.01
$app->format->moneyMinor(12345, 'JPY');                 // ¥12,345
$app->format->moneyMinor(12345, 'KWD');                 // KWD 12.345

    money() accepts a decimal string in major currency units; moneyMinor() accepts an integer in the currency's minor units. Floats are not supported inputs: keep database decimal amounts as strings, and do not compute money with floating-point arithmetic before calling the formatter. The default currency is USD. Pass uppercase three-letter ISO 4217 codes; syntax is checked, but this is not a registry of currently active currencies. Unknown codes use ICU's generic currency formatting.

    ICU supplies standard currency precision: typically 2 digits for USD/EUR, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD, and 4 for CLF. This is not a universal cents conversion. String rounding remains exact even beyond PHP's integer range or Excel's numeric precision; integer minor units are limited to PHP's integer range. Currency position, symbol/code, spacing, negative sign, and digits follow the requested locale. Space characters in the examples above may actually be nonbreaking spaces. No currency conversion, accounting arithmetic, cash rounding increments, or localized-input parsing is performed.

    For all numeric methods, decimal strings use ASCII digits, an optional leading minus, and an optional period followed by fractional digits. No whitespace, leading plus, grouping separators, or exponent notation is accepted. Inputs are limited to 1,024 bytes. Decimal and percentage inputs also reject floats: use strings when fractional precision matters. For example, "0.1" is valid; "1,25", ".5", and "1e3" are not.

    Osoni Templates and Exports

    Every Osoni template and plain PHP view receives the same $format service as $app->format, including layouts, includes, and components:

    BLADE
    {{ $format->date($createdAt, 'long') }}
{{ $format->dateTime($createdAt, timezone: 'America/New_York') }}
{{ $format->money($price, 'USD') }}
{{ $format->moneyMinor($amountInCents, 'USD') }}
{{ $format->decimal($quantity, precision: 3, locale: 'de-DE') }}
{{ $format->percent($completionRatio, precision: 1) }}

    Use normal escaped output. The view-data name format is reserved for this service and cannot override it. Formatting data does not alter template escaping or translate framework-maintained US English copy.

    For documents, pass formatted strings explicitly:

    PHP
    $file = \Osoni\Documents\Documents::excel()
    ->sheet('Report', [
        ['Date', 'Display total', 'Numeric total'],
        [
            $app->format->date($createdAt),
            $app->format->money('1234.50', 'USD'),
            1234.50,
        ],
    ])->build();

    Formatted strings become literal Excel text, not numeric cells. Keep raw numeric cells separate when spreadsheet calculations are needed. JSON numbers must remain locale-independent; emit a separate display string if needed. PDF still has its documented Windows-1252 font limit, so localized digits or spacing outside that character set may require Word instead.

    Structured File Reading

    Read XLSX, CSV, JSON, XML, YAML, and YML with one API after loading bootstrap:

    PHP
    use Osoni\FileReader;

$rows = FileReader::read($app->root . '/storage/import/customers.csv');
$settings = FileReader::read($app->root . '/storage/import/settings.json');
$data = FileReader::read($app->root . '/storage/import/data.txt', [
    'format' => 'json',
    'max_bytes' => 1048576,
    'max_depth' => 32,
]);

    Extensions are case-insensitive. format overrides the extension; supported values are xlsx, csv, json, xml, yaml, and yml. Every read() result is a PHP array, never a parser object. This does not make every format have the same schema: XLSX/CSV produce rows, JSON/YAML preserve their data tree, and XML uses the explicit node structure below. JSON/YAML scalar roots are rejected; empty mappings and lists both become [].

    The static utility is available without an Application instance by explicitly requiring framework/FileReader.php. It does not connect to any service.

    Input safety and limits

    Only existing, readable, regular local files are accepted. Stream wrappers (including HTTP, php://, and phar://) are rejected. Text must be UTF-8; an optional UTF-8 BOM is removed. Convert UTF-16/UTF-32 files to UTF-8 before importing. Readers never evaluate PHP from input.

    The default max_bytes is 16 MiB, including any BOM, even for streamed CSV. Set a positive integer explicitly for larger trusted workloads. max_depth defaults to 64 and accepts 1..256 for XLSX/JSON/XML/YAML; it is not relevant to flat CSV records. XML also limits elements to 100000. YAML normalization limits its traversal to 100000 values/containers to reject cyclic or excessively expanding aliases. Whole-document parsers still need memory for their native parse tree; limits are safeguards, not a process sandbox. Use process memory/time limits appropriate to the workload.

    Authorize paths in your application. Local-file validation is not a directory allowlist, upload validator, schema validator, or permission system. Do not pass arbitrary request paths directly to read(); select authorized private files, validate required fields/types, and escape imported values when rendering. CSV strings beginning with spreadsheet formulas remain unchanged.

    Excel XLSX import and conversion

    The native XLSX reader requires PHP's zip and dom extensions. It reads a single worksheet, selected by zero-based index (default 0) or exact name:

    PHP
    use Osoni\Data;

$data = Data::read($app->root . '/storage/import/customers.xlsx', [
    'sheet' => 'Customers',
    'headers' => true,
]);
$data->write($app->root . '/storage/export/customers.csv');
$data->write($app->root . '/storage/export/customers.json');
$data->write($app->root . '/storage/export/customers.yaml'); // Requires ext-yaml.

    Create the destination directory first; existing files are not overwritten. CSV formula-injection protection is enabled by default and may prefix dangerous cells with an apostrophe. YAML output requires the native ext-yaml extension. All output uses the existing Data writer options and limits.

    The first nonempty row supplies unique, nonempty string headers. Set headers to false for positional rows, or to a list of names to include the first row as data. Blank rows are skipped; missing cells become empty strings. Rows with cells beyond the header width fail. Numbers, including date serials, remain their exact stored strings; booleans become PHP booleans. Shared/inline text and cached formula results are read, but formulas are never calculated. Missing or empty formula caches and Excel error cells fail explicitly. Formatting, date conversion, merged-cell expansion, hidden-row filtering, and legacy .xls are not supported. Validate the workbook and its values for your use.

    The archive is bounded by max_bytes (16 MiB default) and max_uncompressed_bytes (64 MiB default, maximum 256 MiB), with at most 4096 archive entries, 100000 XML elements per part and 100000 returned cells. DTDs, external worksheet relationships, encrypted entries and unsafe archive paths are rejected. Parsing is eager; apply process memory and time limits. iterate() is not supported for XLSX.

    To prepare database inserts, first map headers to an application-owned column allowlist and validate the values. Then use parameterized statements and bindings; do not concatenate values or execute statements selected by a user:

    PHP
    $rows = $data->map(static fn (array $row): array => [
    'name' => $row['name'],
    'email' => $row['email'],
])->validate(['*.name' => 'required|string', '*.email' => 'required|email']);
$statements = $rows->insertStatements('customers', $app->db->driver());
$app->db->transaction(function () use ($app, $statements): void {
    foreach ($statements as $statement) {
        $app->db->execute($statement['sql'], $statement['parameters']);
    }
});

    The sql and parameters pairs can also be exported as JSON with Data::from($statements)->write(...). They are not standalone SQL scripts: execute the SQL with its associated bindings. Only simple identifiers are accepted and quoted for SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server. Identifier quoting is not authorization; choose the table and columns in trusted code. No database changes occur until the application explicitly executes them.

    CSV rows and streaming

    PHP
    $rows = FileReader::read($path, [
    'headers' => true,
    'delimiter' => ';',
    'enclosure' => '"',
    'escape' => '',
    'skip_empty_lines' => true,
]);
// name;email followed by Ada;ada@example.test becomes:
// [['name' => 'Ada', 'email' => 'ada@example.test']]

foreach (FileReader::iterate($path, [
    'headers' => true,
    'max_bytes' => 268435456,
]) as $row) {
    importCustomer($row);
}

    The defaults are comma delimiter, double-quote enclosure, empty escape (standard doubled quotes), headers enabled, and empty physical records skipped. headers: true consumes the first nonblank record as unique nonempty names. Use headers: false for numeric cell lists or headers: ['name', 'email'] to supply names without consuming a record. Records must match the header width. Empty files return []. Cells remain strings, including numbers, booleans, and empty cells.

    Delimiter/enclosure/nonempty escape must be distinct single bytes other than CR, LF, and NUL. For a legacy backslash-escaped file, explicitly set 'escape' => '\\'; native PHP preserves backslash escapes in returned cells. Quoted multiline fields and doubled quotes are supported. Invalid UTF-8, malformed quoting, empty/duplicate headers, and inconsistent header widths produce errors rather than silently dropping data. Whitespace outside closing quotes is rejected by the strict CSV syntax.

    iterate() is lazy: errors may appear after some rows were processed. Choose transaction boundaries/idempotency for partial imports. Memory use is proportional to the largest record, not total row count. The generator closes its file when exhausted or destroyed; unset an iterator you retain after an early break. XLSX, JSON, XML, and YAML currently reject iterate() explicitly rather than pretending to stream a fully buffered document.

    JSON data trees

    JSON objects become associative arrays and JSON lists remain numeric arrays. Nested strings, booleans, nulls, and numbers retain native PHP types. Integers outside PHP's integer range become strings to avoid precision loss; nonfinite float overflow is rejected.

    PHP
    // {"customer":{"name":"Ada","roles":["reader"]}}
$data = FileReader::read($path, ['format' => 'json']);
$name = $data['customer']['name'];

    Invalid JSON throws a RuntimeException explaining the native parse reason, with the original JsonException available through getPrevious(). Neither the message nor XML/YAML diagnostics include source snippets.

    XML nodes, attributes, and namespaces

    XML requires PHP's native DOM extension. Its output always includes the root. Every node has @attributes, @text, and @children; child groups are always lists, even for a single child:

    PHP
    // <catalog><item id="1">Book</item><item id="2"/></catalog>
$data = FileReader::read($path, ['format' => 'xml']);
$items = $data['catalog']['@children']['item'];
$id = $items[0]['@attributes']['id']; // "1"
$text = $items[0]['@text'];           // "Book"

    Nested nodes use the same structure. Direct text/CDATA and whitespace are preserved; comments and processing instructions are ignored. Namespace names use {URI}local, independently of the chosen prefix. For example, <x:item xmlns:x="urn:catalog"/> is keyed by {urn:catalog}item. Namespace declarations are not returned as attributes. Mixed-content text is concatenated and children are grouped by name: this is a data import API, not a lossless XML round-trip representation.

    DTDs and entity declarations are rejected. External resolution and entity substitution are disabled, networking is disabled for libxml, and readers never load schemas or process XInclude. Normal predefined entities such as &amp; work. Do not enable additional entity-loading flags in custom readers.

    YAML and YML setup

    Both extensions use the same YamlReader. There is intentionally no Composer dependency or limited handwritten YAML fallback.

    1. Install the native ext-yaml module compatible with your PHP version, architecture, and thread-safety mode. On Linux, use the distribution's PHP YAML package (for example php-yaml, or a version-specific package). On Windows, use a matching supported PHP YAML extension build and its required LibYAML DLLs.
    2. Enable it in the PHP configuration used for imports (CLI and/or web PHP). Keep yaml.decode_php=0; Osoni rejects an enabled PHP deserializer rather than changing the process's INI configuration.
    3. Verify with php --ri yaml. Restart the web PHP service after INI changes.
    PHP
    $settings = FileReader::read($path, ['format' => 'yaml']);
// name: example
// roles: [reader, editor]
// becomes ['name' => 'example', 'roles' => ['reader', 'editor']]

    Mappings, sequences, nested collections, block strings, anchors/aliases, and merge keys follow the installed ext-yaml/LibYAML semantics (including YAML 1.1 scalar coercions such as yes/no). Quote values that must remain strings. Exactly one mapping/sequence document is accepted. PHP object tags, cyclic or excessively expanding aliases, unsupported PHP value types, nonfinite numbers, scalar roots, and multiple documents fail explicitly. Native INI options for timestamp/binary decoding still apply; do not enable PHP object decoding. Without ext-yaml, YAML reads throw a clear missing-extension exception.

    Errors and additional formats

    Invalid options/unsupported formats throw InvalidArgumentException. Missing, unreadable, oversized files, malformed data, and unavailable extensions throw RuntimeException. No error becomes an empty successful result. Report failures through your application's existing logger/error response; do not expose private paths or imported data to users.

    ExcelReader, CsvReader, JsonReader, XmlReader, and YamlReader live in Osoni\Readers and implement ReaderInterface. Each is usable directly. To add a format, explicitly require trusted application code implementing read(string $path, array $options = []): array and iterate(string $path, array $options = []): iterable. Extending the abstract Osoni\Readers\Reader reuses bounded local-file helpers and the explicit unsupported-streaming exception.

    PHP
    // Treat an application-specific extension as JSON:
FileReader::register('dataset', new \Osoni\Readers\JsonReader());
$data = FileReader::read($app->root . '/storage/import/customer.dataset');

    Registrations are process-local and trusted; they can override built-in format names. Never construct or register reader classes from untrusted file content. No application service/configuration or autoloader is needed for this utility.

    Native File Creation

    Use Osoni\Documents\Documents after loading bootstrap.php; its classes are explicitly registered, with no Composer, autoloading, external programs, or PHP packages. This feature is a PHP API, not a set of CLI commands.

    FactoryOutputSupported content
    Documents::json($data).jsonJSON-serializable values, pretty-printed UTF-8
    Documents::csv($rows).csvIterable lists of scalar cells, configurable delimiter
    Documents::xml($data, 'report').xmlNested arrays mapped to elements
    Documents::pdf().pdfHeadings, paragraphs, fixed-width tables, automatic pagination
    Documents::excel().xlsxMultiple named worksheets and typed cells
    Documents::word().docxHeadings, paragraphs, and bordered tables

    JSON, CSV, and XML factories return a DocumentFile immediately. PDF, Excel, and Word factories return builders; call build() to obtain a DocumentFile. Builders are mutable and chainable. Calling build() does not reset them. Every file exposes read-only contents, mimeType, and extension properties.

    Saving and Downloading

    PHP
    use Osoni\Documents\Documents;

$file = Documents::json(['name' => 'Ada', 'active' => true]);
$file->save($app->root . '/storage/people.json');

// Return this from a web controller action.
return $file->download('people.json');

    save() creates a new local file exclusively: existing files and symlinks are never overwritten. The parent directory must already exist. Relative paths use PHP's current working directory; use an application-root-based path for predictable behavior. Both path separators are accepted. Stream-wrapper URLs, drive-relative Windows paths, control characters, and nonportable basenames are rejected. Files receive 0600 permissions on Linux; restrict inherited ACLs on Windows. Incomplete writes are removed, and failures throw exceptions.

    download() returns a normal Osoni\Response with an attachment disposition, the correct media type and byte length, nosniff, and no-store. UTF-8 filenames use filename* with an ASCII fallback; filenames cannot contain paths or control characters. Give the filename the matching extension. Return the response rather than printing file bytes yourself, so normal HEAD handling and response headers remain intact.

    Register downloads on ordinary web routes, for example:

    PHP
    $router->get('/reports/people.csv', $app->auth->protect(static function (\Osoni\Request $request): \Osoni\Response {
    return \Osoni\Documents\Documents::csv([
        ['Name', 'Active'],
        ['Ada', true],
    ])->download('people.csv');
}));

    Apply the appropriate authentication and record-level authorization before exporting private data. The separate /api/* router still requires JSON responses; it is not a binary-download router.

    JSON, CSV, and XML

    PHP
    use Osoni\Documents\Documents;

Documents::json(['total' => 12.5, 'active' => true, 'notes' => null])
    ->save($app->root . '/storage/report.json');

$rows = [
    ['Name', 'Total', 'Active'],
    ['Ada', 12.5, true],
    ['Lin', null, false],
];
Documents::csv($rows)->save($app->root . '/storage/report.csv');
Documents::csv($rows, delimiter: ';')->save($app->root . '/storage/report-semicolon.csv');

Documents::xml([
    'title' => 'Sales & totals',
    'people' => [
        ['name' => 'Ada', 'total' => 12.5],
        ['name' => 'Lin', 'total' => null],
    ],
], 'report')->save($app->root . '/storage/report.xml');

    CSV uses UTF-8 without a BOM, CRLF record endings, doubled double quotes, and no proprietary backslash escape. Delimiters may be comma, semicolon, tab, or pipe. Rows must be lists, not associative arrays; generators are accepted. Cells accept strings, finite integers/floats, booleans (true/false), and null (an empty cell). CSV has no native type metadata.

    CSV spreadsheet-formula protection is enabled by default. String cells beginning with =, +, -, or @, including after whitespace, or beginning with a tab or line break, receive a leading apostrophe. This intentionally changes those text values; numeric cells remain numeric text. Use protectFormulas: false only for trusted data when an exact raw export is necessary. Importer behavior varies: retain protection when opening untrusted CSV in spreadsheet software.

    XML string keys become element names and integer keys become <item>: the people list above becomes <people><item><name>Ada</name>...</item>...</people>. Null produces an empty element. Element names must be unprefixed ASCII XML names and must not start with xml (case-insensitive). Nesting is limited to 64 levels. Attributes, namespace declarations, raw markup, DTDs, and entities are not accepted as data features. Text is escaped, not interpreted.

    JSON preserves native JSON value types and throws on invalid UTF-8, recursive data, unsupported values, or nonfinite numbers. CSV, XML, and office-document text must be valid UTF-8 containing only XML 1.0 characters; unsupported cell types and nonfinite numbers throw instead of being silently converted.

    Excel Workbooks

    PHP
    use Osoni\Documents\Documents;

$file = Documents::excel()
    ->sheet('People', [
        ['Name', 'Total', 'Active', 'Identifier'],
        ['Ada', 12.5, true, '00123'],
        ['Lin', null, false, '98765432109876543210'],
    ])
    ->sheet('Summary', [['Count', 2]])
    ->build();

$file->save($app->root . '/storage/people.xlsx');
// Or: return $file->download('people.xlsx');

    Requires native zip. Output is a real Office Open XML ZIP package, not HTML renamed to .xls. At least one worksheet is required. Names must be unique without case differences and contain 1 to 31 UTF-16 code units; Excel-reserved characters and leading/trailing apostrophes are rejected. Each worksheet accepts iterable list rows, up to 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns; text cells are limited to 32,767 UTF-16 code units.

    Integers/floats become numeric cells, booleans become boolean cells, null becomes a blank cell, and strings always remain literal text, even when starting with =. Leading zeros are retained in string identifiers. Excel numeric precision is approximately 15 significant digits: pass long identifiers as strings. Dates should be formatted as strings. This baseline does not provide formulas, charts, styling, date-number formats, macros, or reading existing workbooks.

    Word Documents

    PHP
    use Osoni\Documents\Documents;

$file = Documents::word()
    ->heading('Sales report')
    ->paragraph("Prepared by the sales team.\nAll totals are in USD.")
    ->heading('People', 2)
    ->table(['Name', 'Total'], [['Ada', 12.5], ['Lin', null]])
    ->build();

return $file->download('report.docx');

    Requires native zip. Output is a real .docx Office Open XML package. Headings support levels 1 through 6; paragraphs preserve line breaks and tabs. Tables have equal-width columns, borders, a bold repeating header row, and 1 to 63 columns. Every row must match the number of headers. Word handles page layout and pagination. Unicode text is supported, subject to the reader's available fonts. Images, rich inline formatting, page headers/footers, and editing existing documents are outside this baseline.

    PDF Documents

    PHP
    use Osoni\Documents\Documents;

$file = Documents::pdf()
    ->heading('Sales report')
    ->paragraph('Prepared by the sales team. All totals are in USD.')
    ->heading('People', 2)
    ->table(['Name', 'Total'], [['Ada', 12.5], ['Lin', null]])
    ->build();

return $file->download('report.pdf');

    Requires native iconv. The writer produces PDF 1.4 with A4 pages, standard Courier/Courier-Bold fonts, wrapped text, and automatic page breaks. Headings support levels 1 through 3. Tables use fixed-width text columns with separators, support 1 to 10 columns, and wrap long cell values. Table rows may span pages; PDF table headers are not repeated automatically.

    The built-in font supports Windows-1252 text, including common Western European accents and the euro symbol. Other characters throw explicitly rather than producing broken or substituted text; use Word for full Unicode content. This is not an HTML-to-PDF renderer and does not provide embedded fonts, images, complex layouts, encryption, digital signatures, or PDF/A.

    All six formats are assembled in memory; iterable input does not make the result a streaming export. Office packages also use private temporary files, which are removed after creation. Bound export sizes, keep saved files outside public/, and do not pass arbitrary user-selected filesystem paths. Do not treat document creation as permission to expose ORM-hidden fields: select export fields explicitly.

    API and Swagger / OpenAPI

    The backend remains entirely native PHP. The API reserves /api and /api/*; do not place web forms or cookie-authenticated routes here. After php osoni migrate, the following are available:

    MethodPathAccess
    GET / HEAD/api/pingPublic, {"data":{"status":"ok"}}
    GET / HEAD/api/meBearer token of a verified user
    DELETE/api/tokenRevokes the used token, empty HTTP 204
    GET / HEAD/api/docsLocal Swagger UI, if enabled
    GET / HEAD/api/openapi.jsonOpenAPI 3.0.3, if enabled

    Creating, Viewing, and Revoking Tokens

    First register at /register and verify the email address through the existing verification email. Tokens are intentionally issued only through the admin CLI: there is no public password/token endpoint, OAuth server, or additional login without CAPTCHA. Use the numeric ID from the users table, not the email address:

    Terminal
    php osoni api:token 1 laptop 30
php osoni api:tokens 1
php osoni api:revoke 12

    api:token <user-ID> [name] [days] displays the new pbz_... token once. The default expiration is 30 days; the allowed range is 1–365 days. api:tokens displays only the ID, user ID, name, and timestamps, including for expired tokens; api:revoke uses the token ID, not the user ID. Store the token in a secret store, not in source code, query strings, shell history, or shared terminal logs. The database stores only the SHA-256 hash.

    For an API client, send the token in the Authorization header using bearer authentication. Cookies, query parameters, and CSRF tokens never authenticate API requests. A token is valid only while the user exists, the email address is verified, the expiration date has not passed, and the stored session_version matches. Password reset therefore also invalidates all existing API tokens. Web logout removes only the web session; revoke API tokens separately. Tokens have no independent scopes or roles: they represent the user, whose current roles can be checked by an API route guard. Always implement your own per-object authorization; a valid token does not automatically grant access to other users' data.

    Creating an API with the CLI

    Terminal
    php osoni make:api Products
php osoni routes
php osoni api:openapi > openapi.json

    This creates:

    • app/controllers/api/ProductsApiController.php;
    • routes/api/products.php with GET/POST /api/products and GET/PUT/DELETE /api/products/{id};
    • an explicit require in routes/api.php.

    No directory scans, autoloading, or Composer. The route module registers handlers and OpenAPI together through $api->add(). All generated actions require a bearer token by default. They intentionally return HTTP 501 until you implement them: no accidental public CRUD or success message without persistence. Then also replace the generated 501 response descriptions and generic requestBody schemas with your actual fields, responses, and validation. The generator rejects existing files, reserved names, and route conflicts; the registry is locked during the change. Run generators during development, not as a replacement for an atomic production deployment.

    A custom route definition in an explicitly loaded API module:

    PHP
    $api->add('POST', '/api/echo', static function (\Osoni\Request $request): \Osoni\Response {
    $data = \Osoni\Api::validate($request, [
        'message' => 'required|string|min:2|max:200',
    ]);
    $user = $request->apiUser();
    return \Osoni\Response::json(['data' => [
        'message' => $data['message'],
        'user_id' => $user['id'],
    ]]);
}, [
    'summary' => 'Echo a validated message',
    'operationId' => 'echoMessage',
    'requestBody' => ['required' => true, 'content' => [
        'application/json' => ['schema' => [
            'type' => 'object',
            'required' => ['message'],
            'properties' => ['message' => ['type' => 'string', 'minLength' => 2, 'maxLength' => 200]],
        ]],
    ]],
    'responses' => ['200' => ['description' => 'Validated message and current user ID']],
]);

    Pass false as the fifth argument only for intentionally public endpoints. summary, operationId, and responses are required. Path parameters automatically get a required OpenAPI string definition; you can specify them further through parameters. Bearer security is derived from the actual route protection, not from manually set metadata. Every registered API operation appears automatically in Swagger and api:openapi, including operations generated by make:api. To omit an individual operation, pass documented: false to its $api->add() call:

    PHP
    $api->add('GET', '/api/internal', $handler, [
    'summary' => 'Internal status',
    'operationId' => 'internalStatus',
    'responses' => ['200' => ['description' => 'Status']],
], documented: false);

    In a generated module, add documented: false after the metadata array for each action to omit. Metadata remains required; operation IDs must be unique among documented operations. Hiding an operation is not access control: the route remains callable with its normal authentication and authorization. OpenAPI describes the contract but does not perform validation. Api::validate() uses the existing native Validator, returns only the specified fields, and reports invalid input with HTTP 422 and field details. Nested JSON objects remain stdClass; validate them explicitly.

    JSON, Errors, and Limits

    Nonempty API bodies require Content-Type: application/json and a JSON object. Invalid JSON returns 400, other body types 415, and bodies larger than 1 MiB 413. Empty bodies without a JSON content type are allowed, for example with DELETE. Also configure limits in PHP, the web server, and the proxy: PHP may process uploads before application code runs. Normally parsed API requests have a fixed database rate limit of 120 requests per direct client IP per calendar minute; after that, HTTP 429 with Retry-After. Documentation and OpenAPI are exempt and do not require a database. REMOTE_ADDR is used, not unverified proxy headers. Clients behind a proxy therefore share the proxy IP; apply additional limits at the edge. This limit is not DDoS protection.

    API errors consistently use:

    JSON
    {"error":{"code":"HTTP_422","status":422,"message":"Check your input.","details":{"message":["This field is required."]}}}

    details is present only for validation errors. Unknown routes return JSON 404, incorrect methods return JSON 405 with Allow, and missing/invalid tokens return JSON 401 with WWW-Authenticate. Unexpected errors are logged and return a generic JSON 500, even in debug mode. Use Response::json() for custom API responses; for an empty 204, use an empty Response with a JSON content type. API requests do not start a session or set a session cookie. The existing web CSRF check remains unchanged. There is intentionally no automatic CORS or preflight configuration; clients on a different origin require an explicit, carefully restricted policy.

    Local Swagger UI

    Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/docs. Use Authorize with only the pbz_... token; then try GET /api/me, for example. Try it out sends real requests to this server; DELETE /api/token therefore actually revokes the entered token.

    Documentation is enabled by default in local/testing and disabled in production. Override this intentionally with API_DOCS_ENABLED=true or false. This is an availability setting, not access control: also protect production documentation at the proxy/web server level if needed. api:openapi remains available for local export even when HTTP docs are disabled.

    Swagger UI 5.35.0 is official, local, and pinned in public/assets/swagger-ui/; source, integrity, and checksums are listed in VERSION, with the original LICENSE, NOTICE, and JavaScript dependency licenses. No CDN, remote validator, or npm installation is required. Only the documentation page gets its own CSP with local scripts and the inline styles Swagger UI needs; regular web pages retain script-src 'none'. Outgoing documentation requests are restricted to the same origin and /api/. The Swagger client does not send session cookies or store authorization in localStorage/sessionStorage; reloading clears the token. The included assets remain statically public when docs are disabled.

    Validation Component

    The modern validator works on arrays independently of HTTP, sessions, databases, Composer, or an Application instance. Bootstrap loads it explicitly; standalone scripts can require framework/Validator.php.

    PHP
    use Osoni\Validator;

$validator = Validator::make($data, [
    'name' => 'required|string|max:100',
    'email' => 'required|email',
    'age' => 'nullable|integer|min:18',
    'active' => 'boolean',
    'password' => 'required|string|min:8',
]);

if ($validator->fails()) {
    $errors = $validator->errors()->toArray(); // field => list of messages
}
if ($validator->passes()) {
    $validated = $validator->validated();
}

    make() returns a ValidationResult; rules are normalized once, and one evaluation is cached across passes(), fails(), errors(), validated(), and validate(). Unknown/malformed rules throw immediately, even for missing optional fields. Construct a new result for new input.

    The existing static Validator::errors($data, $rules) remains a compatibility API for existing authentication/forms: it supports its original seven rules, messages, Unicode string-size checks, and optional-empty skipping. Use make() for all new rules and the explicit null/missing semantics below.

    Presence, null, and types

    Missing fields skip ordinary value rules. Use required or present when the key must exist:

    RuleMeaning
    requiredExists and is not null, an empty/ASCII-whitespace-only string, or an empty array
    required_if:type,company,nonprofitRequired when another field matches one of these values
    required_unless:type,personRequired unless another field matches; missing comparison fields do not match
    presentKey must exist, even if its value is null
    nullableNull skips value rules, but never overrides a required/present rule
    sometimesIf missing, skip the entire field, including presence rules
    stringValid UTF-8 string; no coercion
    integerPHP integer or signed decimal integer string, within PHP's integer range, without whitespace or leading zeroes except zero itself
    numeric, floatFinite PHP number or decimal/exponent string, without whitespace; integers also qualify
    booleanExactly true, false, 0, 1, "0", or "1"
    arrayPHP array; does not automatically validate/copy children

    0, "0", and false satisfy required. A present null fails string unless nullable is specified; a present empty string passes string but fails integer/email. No automatic trimming, string-to-number conversion, HTML stripping, or null conversion occurs.

    For conditional comparison lists, string/integer/float values compare by their exact string representation. Booleans match only true/false literals and null matches only null; false never silently equals zero.

    Sizes, strings, formatting, and comparisons

    RulesMeaning
    min:n, max:n, between:min,maxInclusive numeric magnitude for native numbers or fields with integer/numeric/float rules; otherwise Unicode code-point length for strings or item count for arrays
    length:nExact string code-point length or array count
    regex:/pattern/uNative PCRE match; invalid patterns and engine/resource errors throw explicitly
    alpha, alpha_numNonempty Unicode letters, or letters/numbers; spaces, punctuation and combining marks outside those categories do not qualify
    emailNative FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL
    urlAbsolute HTTP(S) URL without credentials, whitespace, controls, or backslashes
    uuidCanonical hyphenated UUID with version 1..8 and RFC variant bits
    ip, ipv4, ipv6Native IP address validation, optionally restricted to one family
    jsonSyntactically valid JSON string, depth at most 64; scalar JSON is permitted
    same:other, different:otherStrict PHP identity/nonidentity; comparison field must exist
    in:a,b, not_in:a,bMembership/nonmembership using the conditional-list comparison semantics above
    confirmedStrict equality to the sibling field_confirmation value

    Rules accept pipe strings or lists of individual rule strings/objects:

    PHP
    $validator = Validator::make($data, [
    'name' => ['required', 'string', 'max:100'],
    'pet' => ['string', 'regex:/^(cat|dog)$/u'],
]);

    Use **array syntax for regex patterns containing |**, so alternation is not mistaken for a rule separator. Patterns are trusted application configuration, not user-supplied expressions. PCRE's configured resource limits still apply. Size arguments accept finite signed/decimal bounds; length and max_size require nonnegative integers. Integer bounds within PHP's integer range compare as integers; decimal/out-of-range magnitudes use PHP floating-point precision, not arbitrary-precision financial arithmetic.

    Dates

    date accepts strict YYYY-MM-DD or ISO timestamps with T, seconds, optional fractional seconds, and optional Z/numeric offset. Invalid calendar dates and rollover times fail. Timezone-less input uses UTC independently of the global PHP timezone. Relative strings such as tomorrow are not accepted.

    PHP
    $data = Validator::make($input, [
    'start' => 'required|date',
    'end' => 'required|date|after:@start|before:2030-01-01',
    'display_date' => 'date_format:d/m/Y',
])->validate();

    before/after are exclusive and accept an ISO literal or explicit @field reference; referenced fields must contain valid ISO dates. date_format uses native PHP date-format characters with exact round-trip matching. Do not combine date with a non-ISO date_format expecting conversion.

    Nested data, wildcard arrays, and filtered output

    PHP
    $data = Validator::make($input, [
    'user' => 'required|array',
    'user.name' => 'required|string',
    'user.email' => 'required|email',
    'users' => 'required|array|min:1|max:100',
    'users.*.email' => 'required|email',
    'tags' => 'array',
    'tags.*' => 'string|max:30',
])->validate();

    Errors use concrete paths such as users.1.email. Comparison-field wildcards are resolved at the same indexes, for example users.*.end => after:@users.*.start. Dot paths traverse arrays only. Dots/asterisks inside literal keys are not supported; map such imported keys to simple field names first. Empty arrays expand to no wildcard matches: require and bound the parent array separately. Wildcards are never a substitute for validating the container's type.

    Array rules validate containers, not all their descendants. Validated output starts each covered array as [], then copies only covered descendants. For example, validating user => array and user.email => email excludes user.admin. A standalone user => array produces user => []; add rules for every permitted child or user.* for all permitted scalar children. This intentional filtering also applies to the Request/API adapters. Array keys/indexes are preserved, including sparse numeric indexes.

    Missing optional fields are omitted. Present allowed nulls remain null. No partial output is returned on failure: both validated() and validate() throw ValidationException when any field is invalid.

    Error messages and field labels

    PHP
    $validator = Validator::make($input,
    ['email_address' => 'required|email', 'users.*.email' => 'email'],
    [
        'email_address.required' => 'An email address is required.',
        'email_address.email' => 'Please provide a valid :attribute.',
        'users.*.email.email' => 'Please check this row email.',
    ],
    ['email_address' => 'email address'],
);

$errors = $validator->errors();
